originalComment: Removes all attributes from the request as well as clears entries in this map.
codeComment: Summary: The `clear` method overrides the existing method to reset the `entries` to `null` and iteratively removes all attributes by iterating through the attribute names and calling `removeAttribute` on each.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void clear () { entries = null;Iterator < String > keys = getAttributeNames ();while (keys.hasNext ()) { removeAttribute (keys.next ());} }

originalComment: Returns a Set of attributes from the http request.
codeComment: The method `entrySet()` is overridden to return a `Set` of `Entry<String, Object>` objects. If the `entries` set is `null`, it initializes a new `HashSet` and populates it with entries from the attributes. It retrieves attribute names using `getAttributeNames()` and for each attribute name, it fetches the corresponding attribute value using `getAttribute(key)`. Each entry is an anonymous class implementing the `Entry<String, Object>` interface, which overrides methods such as `equals()`, `hashCode()`, `getKey()`, `getValue()`, and `setValue()`. The `setValue()` method also updates the attribute value using `setAttribute(key, obj)`. Finally, the method returns the populated `entries` set.
codeFunctions: @ Override public Set < Entry < String,Object > > entrySet () { if (entries == null) { entries = new HashSet <> ();Iterator < String > iterator = getAttributeNames ();while (iterator.hasNext ()) { final String key = iterator.next ();final Object value = getAttribute (key);entries.add (new Entry < String,Object > () { @ Override public boolean equals (final Object obj) { if (obj == null) { return false;} if (this.getClass () != obj.getClass ()) { return false;} Entry entry = (Entry) obj;return ((key == null)?(entry.getKey () == null):key.equals (entry.getKey ())) && ((value == null)?(entry.getValue () == null):value.equals (entry.getValue ()));} @ Override public int hashCode () { return ((key == null)?0:key.hashCode ()) ^ ((value == null)?0:value.hashCode ());} @ Override public String getKey () { return key;} @ Override public Object getValue () { return value;} @ Override public Object setValue (final Object obj) { setAttribute (key,obj);return value;} });} } return entries;}

originalComment: Saves an attribute in the request.
codeComment: Summary: This method overrides the `put` method to store a key-value pair. It first sets the `entries` variable to `null`, retrieves the previous value associated with the key using the `get` method, sets the new value for the key using the `setAttribute` method, and then returns the previous value.
codeFunctions: @ Override public Object put (final String key,final Object value) { entries = null;Object previous = get (key);setAttribute (key,value);return previous;}

originalComment: Removes the specified request attribute.
codeComment: Summary: The `remove` method overrides the superclass method to remove an entry associated with the specified key. It first sets the `entries` field to `null`, retrieves the value associated with the key using the `get` method, removes the attribute by converting the key to a string and calling `removeAttribute`, and finally returns the retrieved value.
codeFunctions: @ Override public Object remove (final Object key) { entries = null;Object value = get (key);removeAttribute (key.toString ());return value;}

originalComment: Returns current stack trace in form of array of stack trace elements.First stack trace element is removed.Since an exception is thrown internally this method is slow.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `getCurrentStackTrace` retrieves the current stack trace and returns it as an array of `StackTraceElement`, excluding the first element which represents the call to `getCurrentStackTrace` itself. If the stack trace has only one element, it returns the original stack trace array.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ({ "ThrowCaughtLocally" }) public static StackTraceElement [ ] getCurrentStackTrace () { StackTraceElement [ ] ste = new Exception ().getStackTrace ();if (ste.length > 1) { StackTraceElement [ ] result = new StackTraceElement [ ste.length - 1 ];System.arraycopy (ste,1,result,0,ste.length - 1);return result;} else { return ste;} }

originalComment: Returns stack trace filtered by class names.
codeComment: The method `getStackTrace` filters the stack trace of a given `Throwable` object based on allow and deny lists of class names. It iterates through each `StackTraceElement` in the stack trace, checks if the class name of the element contains any of the strings in the `allow` list (if provided), and skips the element if it does not match any. Additionally, it skips elements whose class names contain any of the strings in the `deny` list (if provided). The filtered elements are collected into an `ArrayList`, which is then converted to an array of `StackTraceElement` and returned.
codeFunctions: public static StackTraceElement [ ] getStackTrace (final Throwable t,final String [ ] allow,final String [ ] deny) { StackTraceElement [ ] st = t.getStackTrace ();ArrayList < StackTraceElement > result = new ArrayList <> (st.length);elementLoop:for (StackTraceElement element:st) { String className = element.getClassName ();if (allow != null) { boolean validElemenet = false;for (String filter:allow) { if (className.contains (filter)) { validElemenet = true;break;} } if (!validElemenet) { continue;} } if (deny != null) { for (String filter:deny) { if (className.contains (filter)) { continue elementLoop;} } } result.add (element);} st = new StackTraceElement [ result.size () ];return result.toArray (st);}

originalComment: Returns stack trace chain filtered by class names.
codeComment: The method `getStackTraceChain` takes a `Throwable` object and two arrays of strings (`allow` and `deny`) as parameters. It iterates through the exception chain starting from the given `Throwable` and its subsequent causes. For each `Throwable` in the chain, it retrieves the stack trace filtered by the `allow` and `deny` lists using the `getStackTrace` method (assumed to be defined elsewhere). The filtered stack traces are collected in an `ArrayList` of `StackTraceElement` arrays. Finally, the method converts this `ArrayList` into a 2D array of `StackTraceElement` arrays and returns it, representing the stack trace chain for the entire exception hierarchy.
codeFunctions: public static StackTraceElement [ ] [ ] getStackTraceChain (Throwable t,final String [ ] allow,final String [ ] deny) { ArrayList < StackTraceElement [ ] > result = new ArrayList <> ();while (t != null) { StackTraceElement [ ] stack = getStackTrace (t,allow,deny);result.add (stack);t = t.getCause ();} StackTraceElement [ ] [ ] allStacks = new StackTraceElement [ result.size () ] [  ];for (int i = 0;i < allStacks.length;i ++) { allStacks [ i ] = result.get (i);} return allStacks;}

originalComment: Returns exception chain starting from top up to root cause.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `getExceptionChain` takes a `Throwable` object as input and returns an array of `Throwable` objects representing the exception chain. It initializes an `ArrayList` to store the exceptions, starting with the input `Throwable`. It then iteratively adds each subsequent cause of the exception (obtained via `getCause()`) to the list until there are no more causes. Finally, it converts the `ArrayList` to an array and returns it.
codeFunctions: public static Throwable [ ] getExceptionChain (Throwable throwable) { ArrayList < Throwable > list = new ArrayList <> ();list.add (throwable);while ((throwable = throwable.getCause ()) != null) { list.add (throwable);} Throwable [ ] result = new Throwable [ list.size () ];return list.toArray (result);}

originalComment: Prints stack trace into a String.
codeComment: This method, `exceptionStackTraceToString`, takes a `Throwable` object as input and converts its stack trace into a `String`. It uses a `StringWriter` and a `PrintWriter` to capture the stack trace output. After printing the stack trace to the `PrintWriter`, it closes both the `PrintWriter` and `StringWriter` using a utility method `StreamUtil.close`. Finally, it returns the stack trace as a `String` by calling `toString` on the `StringWriter`.
codeFunctions: public static String exceptionStackTraceToString (final Throwable t) { StringWriter sw = new StringWriter ();PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter (sw,true);t.printStackTrace (pw);StreamUtil.close (pw);StreamUtil.close (sw);return sw.toString ();}

originalComment: Prints full exception stack trace from top to root cause into a String.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `exceptionChainToString` takes a `Throwable` object as input and returns a string representation of the entire exception chain. It uses a `StringWriter` and a `PrintWriter` to capture the stack traces of the exception and its causes. The method iterates through the exception chain by repeatedly calling `getCause()` on the `Throwable` object until there are no more causes. After capturing all stack traces, it closes the `PrintWriter` and `StringWriter` using `StreamUtil.close()` and returns the concatenated stack traces as a single string.
codeFunctions: public static String exceptionChainToString (Throwable t) { StringWriter sw = new StringWriter ();PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter (sw,true);while (t != null) { t.printStackTrace (pw);t = t.getCause ();} StreamUtil.close (pw);StreamUtil.close (sw);return sw.toString ();}

originalComment: Build a message for the given base message and its cause.
codeComment: The `buildMessage` method constructs a detailed error message by appending the root cause of a `Throwable` to a given message. If a `Throwable` is provided, it retrieves the root cause using the `getRootCause` method, then appends this root cause to the original message, separated by "; <--- ". If no `Throwable` is provided, it simply returns the original message.
codeFunctions: public static String buildMessage (final String message,Throwable cause) { if (cause != null) { cause = getRootCause (cause);StringBuilder buf = new StringBuilder ();if (message != null) { buf.append (message).append ("; ");} buf.append ("<--- ").append (cause);return buf.toString ();} else { return message;} }

originalComment: Unwraps invocation and undeclared exceptions to real cause.
codeComment: The method `unwrapThrowable` takes a `Throwable` object as input and iteratively unwraps it if it is an instance of `InvocationTargetException` or `UndeclaredThrowableException`. It returns the underlying cause of the exception by repeatedly accessing the target or undeclared throwable until it reaches a `Throwable` that is not one of these types.
codeFunctions: public static Throwable unwrapThrowable (final Throwable wrappedThrowable) { Throwable unwrapped = wrappedThrowable;while (true) { if (unwrapped instanceof InvocationTargetException) { unwrapped = ((InvocationTargetException) unwrapped).getTargetException ();} else if (unwrapped instanceof UndeclaredThrowableException) { unwrapped = ((UndeclaredThrowableException) unwrapped).getUndeclaredThrowable ();} else { return unwrapped;} } }

originalComment: Parses class name that matches madvoc - related names.
codeComment: The method `registerAsConsumer` takes a `ClassScanner` object as a parameter and registers a consumer that processes each `classPathEntry`. For each entry, it checks if the entry name ends with a specified `actionClassSuffix`. If it does, it attempts to load the class and pass it to `acceptActionClass`. If an exception occurs during this process, it logs a debug message indicating an invalid Madvoc action. If the entry does not end with the `actionClassSuffix` but uses a specific type signature (`MADVOC_COMPONENT_ANNOTATION`), it attempts to load the class and pass it to `acceptMadvocComponentClass`. If an exception occurs here, it logs a debug message indicating an invalid Madvoc component.
codeFunctions: protected void registerAsConsumer (final ClassScanner classScanner) { classScanner.registerEntryConsumer (classPathEntry -> { final String entryName = classPathEntry.name ();if (entryName.endsWith (actionClassSuffix)) { try { acceptActionClass (classPathEntry.loadClass ());} catch (Exception ex) { log.debug ("Invalid Madvoc action, ignoring: " + entryName);} } else if (classPathEntry.isTypeSignatureInUse (MADVOC_COMPONENT_ANNOTATION)) { try { acceptMadvocComponentClass (classPathEntry.loadClass ());} catch (Exception ex) { log.debug ("Invalid Madvoc component ignoring: {}" + entryName);} } });}

originalComment: Registers new Madvoc component.
codeComment: Summary: The method `acceptMadvocComponentClass` takes a `Class` object as a parameter. It first checks if the provided class is `null` and returns immediately if it is. Then, it verifies the class using the `checkClass` method, returning if the check fails. If the class passes the check, it adds a lambda expression to the `madvocComponents` list, which, when executed, registers the component class with the `madvocContainer`.
codeFunctions: protected void acceptMadvocComponentClass (final Class componentClass) { if (componentClass == null) { return;} if (!checkClass (componentClass)) { return;} madvocComponents.add (() -> madvocContainer.registerComponent (componentClass));}

originalComment: Returns system class loader.
codeComment: This method, `getSystemClassLoader`, retrieves the system class loader. It first checks if a security manager is present. If no security manager is active, it directly returns the system class loader using `ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader()`. If a security manager is present, it uses `AccessController.doPrivileged` to execute the same operation with the necessary privileges, ensuring that the system class loader can be accessed securely.
codeFunctions: public static ClassLoader getSystemClassLoader () { if (System.getSecurityManager () == null) { return ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader ();} else { return AccessController.doPrivileged ((PrivilegedAction < ClassLoader >) ClassLoader :: getSystemClassLoader);} }

originalComment: Opens a resource of the specified name for reading.
codeComment: This method, `getResourceAsStream`, takes a resource name and a class loader as parameters. It attempts to retrieve a URL for the specified resource using the provided class loader. If the URL is successfully obtained, it opens an input stream from the URL and returns it. If the URL is null, indicating that the resource could not be found, the method returns null.
codeFunctions: public static InputStream getResourceAsStream (final String resourceName,final ClassLoader callingClass) throws IOException { URL url = getResourceUrl (resourceName,callingClass);if (url != null) { return url.openStream ();} return null;}

originalComment: Opens a resource of the specified name for reading.Controls caching that is important when the same jar is reloaded using custom classloader.
codeComment: This method, `getResourceAsStream`, retrieves an `InputStream` for a specified resource using a given `ClassLoader`. It accepts three parameters: the name of the resource (`resourceName`), the `ClassLoader` to use (`callingClass`), and a boolean indicating whether to use caching (`useCache`). The method first attempts to obtain a `URL` for the resource. If the `URL` is not null, it opens a connection to the `URL`, sets the caching behavior based on the `useCache` parameter, and returns an `InputStream` from the connection. If the `URL` is null, the method returns null.
codeFunctions: public static InputStream getResourceAsStream (final String resourceName,final ClassLoader callingClass,final boolean useCache) throws IOException { URL url = getResourceUrl (resourceName,callingClass);if (url != null) { URLConnection urlConnection = url.openConnection ();urlConnection.setUseCaches (useCache);return urlConnection.getInputStream ();} return null;}

originalComment: Opens a class of the specified name for reading using class classloader.
codeComment: Summary: This method, `getClassAsStream`, takes a `Class` object as input and returns an `InputStream` for the resource associated with that class. It converts the class name to a file name using `ClassUtil.convertClassNameToFileName` and retrieves the resource using `getResourceAsStream` with the class's class loader. If an `IOException` occurs during the process, it is thrown.
codeFunctions: public static InputStream getClassAsStream (final Class clazz) throws IOException { return getResourceAsStream (ClassUtil.convertClassNameToFileName (clazz),clazz.getClassLoader ());}

originalComment: Opens a class of the specified name for reading using provided class loader.
codeComment: Summary: This method, `getClassAsStream`, takes a class name and a class loader as parameters. It converts the class name to a file name using the `ClassUtil.convertClassNameToFileName` method and then retrieves an `InputStream` for the resource using the `getResourceAsStream` method with the converted file name and the provided class loader. originalComment: Adds a new child to the tree.
codeComment: The method `add` takes a `String` parameter `newValue` and creates a new `RouteChunk` object with it, along with the current `routes` and `this` object. If the `children` array is `null`, it initializes it with the new `RouteChunk`. Otherwise, it appends the new `RouteChunk` to the existing `children` array using `ArraysUtil.append`. Finally, it returns the newly created `RouteChunk`.
codeFunctions: public RouteChunk add (final String newValue) { RouteChunk routeChunk = new RouteChunk (routes,this,newValue);if (children == null) { children = new RouteChunk [ ] { routeChunk };} else { children = ArraysUtil.append (children,routeChunk);} return routeChunk;}

originalComment: Finds existing chunk or creates a new one if does not exist.
codeComment: The method `findOrCreateChild` takes a `String` value as input and checks if there are any existing children. If children exist, it iterates through them to find a child whose value matches the input. If a match is found, it returns that child. If no match is found or if there are no children, it adds a new child with the input value and returns it.
codeFunctions: public RouteChunk findOrCreateChild (final String value) { if (children != null) { for (RouteChunk child:children) { if (child.get ().equals (value)) { return child;} } } return add (value);}

originalComment: Checks if request if multi - part and parse it.If request is not multi - part it copies all parameters to make usage the same in both cases.
codeComment: The `parseRequest` method processes an HTTP request. If the request is a multipart request, it parses the request stream using the `parseRequestStream` method with the request's input stream and character encoding. Otherwise, it iterates through the request's parameter names, retrieves the values for each parameter, and stores them using the `putParameters` method.
codeFunctions: public void parseRequest () throws IOException { if (ServletUtil.isMultipartRequest (request)) { parseRequestStream (request.getInputStream (),characterEncoding);} else { Enumeration names = request.getParameterNames ();while (names.hasMoreElements ()) { String paramName = (String) names.nextElement ();String [ ] values = request.getParameterValues (paramName);putParameters (paramName,values);} } }

originalComment: Converter to collection.
codeComment: Summary: The `convertToCollection` method takes an object, a destination type, and a component type as parameters. It uses the `typeConverterManager` to convert the provided object into a collection of the specified destination type and component type, then returns the resulting collection. The method is annotated with `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` to suppress unchecked type conversion warnings.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") protected Object convertToCollection (final Object value,final Class destinationType,final Class componentType) { return typeConverterManager.convertToCollection (value,destinationType,componentType);}

originalComment: Invokes setter but first converts type to match the setter type.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `invokeSetter` method is designed to invoke a setter on a bean property with a given value. It performs several operations to ensure the value is correctly formatted and compatible with the setter's expected type. Here's a step-by-step summary:

1. **Mapper Function Application**: If a `MapperFunction` is associated with the setter, it is applied to transform the input value.
2. **Type Checking**: The method checks if the setter's type is a `Collection`. If it is, it further determines the component type of the collection.
3. **Value Conversion**:
   - If the type is a `Collection`, the value is converted to a collection of the appropriate type and component type.
   - If the type is not a `Collection`, the value is converted to the expected type.
4. **Setter Invocation**: The transformed value is then passed to the setter method of the bean property.
5. **Exception Handling**: If an exception occurs during the process, it is caught. If the method is not in silent mode, a `BeanException` is thrown with a descriptive message. Otherwise, the method returns `null`.
6. **Return Value**: The method returns the final value that was set on the bean property.
codeFunctions: protected Object invokeSetter (final Setter setter,final BeanProperty bp,Object value) { try { final MapperFunction setterMapperFunction = setter.getMapperFunction ();if (setterMapperFunction != null) { value = setterMapperFunction.apply (value);} final Class type = setter.getSetterRawType ();if (ClassUtil.isTypeOf (type,Collection.class)) { Class componentType = setter.getSetterRawComponentType ();value = convertToCollection (value,type,componentType);} else { // no collections value = convertType (value,type);} setter.invokeSetter (bp.bean,value);} catch (Exception ex) { if (isSilent) { return null;} throw new BeanException ("Setter failed: " + setter,ex);} return value;}

originalComment: Sets the array element forced.If index is greater then arrays length array will be expanded to the index.If speed is critical it is better to allocate an array with proper size before using this method.
codeComment: Summary: The `arrayForcedSet` method sets a value in an array at a specified index, ensuring the array is large enough and converting the value to the correct type if necessary. It takes a `BeanProperty`, an array, an index, and a value as parameters. The method first determines the component type of the array, then ensures the array is of sufficient size using `ensureArraySize`. It converts the value to the appropriate type using `convertType`, and finally sets the value in the array at the given index using `Array.set`.
codeFunctions: protected void arrayForcedSet (final BeanProperty bp,Object array,final int index,Object value) { Class componentType = array.getClass ().getComponentType ();array = ensureArraySize (bp,array,componentType,index);value = convertType (value,componentType);Array.set (array,index,value);}

originalComment: Creates new instance for current property name through its setter.It uses default constructor!
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `createBeanProperty` method is responsible for creating and initializing a new instance of a property based on the provided `BeanProperty` object. It first retrieves the setter for the property. If no setter is found, it returns `null`. It then determines the raw type of the setter and attempts to create a new instance of this type using `ClassUtil.newInstance`. If an exception occurs during instantiation, it either returns `null` if the method is set to be silent or throws a `BeanException` with details about the failure. If the instantiation is successful, it invokes the setter on the new instance with the provided `BeanProperty` and returns the newly created and initialized instance.
codeFunctions: protected Object createBeanProperty (final BeanProperty bp) { Setter setter = bp.getSetter (true);if (setter == null) { return null;} Class type = setter.getSetterRawType ();Object newInstance;try { newInstance = ClassUtil.newInstance (type);} catch (Exception ex) { if (isSilent) { return null;} throw new BeanException ("Invalid property: " + bp.name,bp,ex);} newInstance = invokeSetter (setter,bp,newInstance);return newInstance;}

originalComment: Extracts type of current property.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `extractType` method is designed to determine the type of a property from a `BeanProperty` object. It first retrieves the `Getter` associated with the property, considering whether it is declared. If a `Getter` is found, it checks if the property has an index. If an index is present, it attempts to get the raw component type of the getter. If this type is `null`, it defaults to `Object.class`. If no index is present, it simply returns the raw type of the getter. If no `Getter` is found, the method returns `null`, although this scenario is noted as unexpected.
codeFunctions: protected Class extractType (final BeanProperty bp) { Getter getter = bp.getGetter (isDeclared);if (getter != null) { if (bp.index != null) { Class type = getter.getGetterRawComponentType ();return type == null?Object.class:type;} return getter.getGetterRawType ();} return null;// this should not happens }

originalComment: Stops the user session by removing it from the http session and invalidating the cookie.
codeComment: The method `stop` is designed to terminate a user session by removing the authentication session attribute and invalidating the authentication cookie. It first attempts to retrieve the current HTTP session from the `HttpServletRequest` object without creating a new one if it doesn't exist. If a session is found, it removes the attribute identified by `AUTH_SESSION_NAME`. Next, it looks for a cookie named `AUTH_COOKIE_NAME` in the request. If the cookie is present, it sets the cookie's maximum age to 0, effectively deleting it, and sets its path to the root ("/"). Finally, it adds the modified cookie to the `HttpServletResponse` to ensure the client's browser removes the cookie.

It first determines whether to scan accessible methods or only supported methods based on the `classDescriptor` configuration. For each identified property, it creates a `MethodDescriptor` and adds it to a `HashMap` with the property name as the key. If configured, it also includes non-static fields as properties, applying any specified prefixes to field names before adding them to the map. It retrieves all action runtimes and aliases from the `ActionsManager` component of the `webApp`. If there are no actions, it returns immediately. For each action, it prints the action method, action path, and a signature composed of the class name and method name. codeFunctions: protected void printRoutes (final int width) { final ActionsManager actionsManager = webApp.madvocContainer ().lookupComponent (ActionsManager.class);final List < ActionRuntime > actions = actionsManager.getAllActionRuntimes ();final Map < String,String > aliases = actionsManager.getAllAliases ();if (actions.isEmpty ()) { return;} final Print print = new Print ();print.line ("Routes",width);actions.stream ().sorted (Comparator.comparing (actionRuntime -> actionRuntime.getActionPath () + ' ' + actionRuntime.getActionMethod ())).forEach (ar -> { final String actionMethod = ar.getActionMethod ();print.out (Chalk256.chalk ().yellow (),actionMethod == null?"*":actionMethod,7);print.space ();final String signature = ClassUtil.getShortClassName (ProxettaUtil.resolveTargetClass (ar.getActionClass ()),2) + ' ' + ar.getActionClassMethod ().getName ();print.outLeftRightNewLine (Chalk256.chalk ().green (),ar.getActionPath (),Chalk256.chalk ().blue (),signature,width - 7 - 1);});if (!aliases.isEmpty ()) { print.line ("Aliases",width);actions.stream ().sorted (Comparator.comparing (actionRuntime -> actionRuntime.getActionPath () + ' ' + actionRuntime.getActionMethod ())).forEach (ar -> { final String actionPath = ar.getActionPath ();for (final Map.Entry < String,String > entry:aliases.entrySet ()) { if (entry.getValue ().equals (actionPath)) { print.space (8);print.outLeftRightNewLine (Chalk256.chalk ().green (),entry.getValue (),Chalk256.chalk ().blue (),entry.getKey (),width - 8);} } });} print.line (width);}

originalComment: Encrypts complete content block by block.
codeComment: The method `encrypt` takes a byte array `content` as input and encrypts it using a block cipher approach. It initializes a `FastByteBuffer` to store the encrypted data. The method calculates the number of full blocks and any remaining bytes that do not fill a complete block. It iterates over each full block, encrypts it using the `encryptBlock` method, and appends the encrypted block to the `FastByteBuffer`. If there are remaining bytes that do not fill a complete block, it pads these bytes with a terminator and encrypts the resulting block. Finally, it returns the encrypted data as a byte array.
codeFunctions: public byte [ ] encrypt (final byte [ ] content) { FastByteBuffer fbb = new FastByteBuffer ();int length = content.length + 1;int blockCount = length / blockSizeInBytes;int remaining = length;int offset = 0;for (int i = 0;i < blockCount;i ++) { if (remaining == blockSizeInBytes) { break;} byte [ ] encrypted = encryptBlock (content,offset);fbb.append (encrypted);offset += blockSizeInBytes;remaining -= blockSizeInBytes;} if (remaining != 0) { // process remaining bytes byte [ ] block = new byte [ blockSizeInBytes ];System.arraycopy (content,offset,block,0,remaining - 1);block [ remaining - 1 ] = TERMINATOR;byte [ ] encrypted = encryptBlock (block,0);fbb.append (encrypted);} return fbb.toArray ();}

originalComment: Decrypts the whole content block by block.
codeComment: The method `decrypt` takes an array of encrypted bytes as input and returns the decrypted content as a byte array. It uses a `FastByteBuffer` to efficiently build the output. The method processes the input in blocks of a fixed size (`blockSizeInBytes`). For each block except the last one, it decrypts the block and appends it to the `FastByteBuffer`. For the last block, it decrypts the block and then trims any padding by finding a terminator byte (`TERMINATOR`) and only appending the bytes up to (but not including) the terminator. Finally, it converts the `FastByteBuffer` to a byte array and returns it.
codeFunctions: public byte [ ] decrypt (final byte [ ] encryptedContent) { FastByteBuffer fbb = new FastByteBuffer ();int length = encryptedContent.length;int blockCount = length / blockSizeInBytes;int offset = 0;for (int i = 0;i < blockCount - 1;i ++) { byte [ ] decrypted = decryptBlock (encryptedContent,offset);fbb.append (decrypted);offset += blockSizeInBytes;} // process last block byte [ ] decrypted = decryptBlock (encryptedContent,offset);// find terminator int ndx = blockSizeInBytes - 1;while (ndx >= 0) { if (decrypted [ ndx ] == TERMINATOR) { break;} ndx --;} fbb.append (decrypted,0,ndx);return fbb.toArray ();}

originalComment: Converts map to target type.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `map2bean` method converts a `Map` object into a Java bean of a specified target type. It performs the following steps:

1. **Determine Target Type**: 
   - If the `map` contains a key that specifies the class name (`classMetadataName`), it attempts to load the corresponding class.
   - If the class name is not found in the map and `targetType` is not provided, the method returns the original map.
   - If the class name is found but the class cannot be loaded, a `JsonException` is thrown.

2. **Create Target Instance**:
   - If the target type is determined, an instance of the target type is created using `jsonParser.newObjectInstance`.

3. **Introspect Target Class**:
   - The method uses `ClassIntrospector` to get a `ClassDescriptor` for the target class, which provides information about the class's properties.

4. **Iterate Over Map Entries**:
   - For each key-value pair in the map:
     - If the key is the class metadata name, it is skipped.
     - The method retrieves the `PropertyDescriptor` for the key from the `ClassDescriptor`.
     - If the target is not a `Map` and the property descriptor is not found, the key-value pair is skipped.
     - The value is processed based on its type:
       - If the value is a `List`, it is generified if the property type is not a `String`.
       - If the value is a `Map`, it is recursively converted to a bean if the target property is not a `Map`. If the target is also a `Map`, it is generified if necessary.

5. **Set Values**:
   - If the target is a `Map`, the key-value pair is added to the map.
   - Otherwise, the value is set on the target bean using the `PropertyDescriptor`.

6. **Return Target**:
   - The method returns the populated target object, which could be a bean or a map depending on the input and processing.
codeFunctions: public Object map2bean (final Map map,Class targetType) { Object target = null;// create targets type String className = (String) map.get (classMetadataName);if (className == null) { if (targetType == null) { // nothing to do, no information about target type found target = map;} } else { checkClassName (jsonParser.classnameWhitelist,className);try { targetType = ClassLoaderUtil.loadClass (className);} catch (ClassNotFoundException cnfex) { throw new JsonException (cnfex);} } if (target == null) { target = jsonParser.newObjectInstance (targetType);} ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (target.getClass ());boolean targetIsMap = target instanceof Map;for (Object key:map.keySet ()) { String keyName = key.toString ();if (classMetadataName != null) { if (keyName.equals (classMetadataName)) { continue;} } PropertyDescriptor pd = cd.getPropertyDescriptor (keyName,declared);if (!targetIsMap && pd == null) { // target property does not exist, continue continue;} // value is one of JSON basic types, like Number, Map, List... Object value = map.get (key);Class propertyType = pd == null?null:pd.getType ();Class componentType = pd == null?null:pd.resolveComponentType (true);if (value != null) { if (value instanceof List) { if (componentType != null && componentType != String.class) { value = generifyList ((List) value,componentType);} } else if (value instanceof Map) { // if the value we want to inject is a Map... if (!ClassUtil.isTypeOf (propertyType,Map.class)) { // ... and if target is NOT a map value = map2bean ((Map) value,propertyType);} else { // target is also a Map, but we might need to generify it Class keyType = pd == null?null:pd.resolveKeyType (true);if (keyType != String.class || componentType != String.class) { // generify value = generifyMap ((Map) value,keyType,componentType);} } } } if (targetIsMap) { ((Map) target).put (keyName,value);} else { try { setValue (target,pd,value);} catch (Exception ignore) { ignore.printStackTrace ();} } } return target;}

codeComment: The method `generifyList` takes a `List` and a `Class` object representing the component type. It iterates through each element of the list. If an element is not null, it checks if the element is an instance of `Map`. If it is, the method converts the map to a bean of the specified component type using the `map2bean` method and replaces the element in the list with the bean. If the element is not a map, it converts the element to the specified component type using the `convert` method and replaces the element in the list with the converted value. Finally, the method returns the modified list.
codeFunctions: private Object generifyList (final List list,final Class componentType) { for (int i = 0;i < list.size ();i ++) { Object element = list.get (i);if (element != null) { if (element instanceof Map) { Object bean = map2bean ((Map) element,componentType);list.set (i,bean);} else { Object value = convert (element,componentType);list.set (i,value);} } } return list;}

originalComment: Change map elements to match key and value types.
codeComment: The method `generifyMap` takes a `Map<Object, Object>` and converts it to a `Map<K, V>` by changing the types of keys and values based on the provided `keyType` and `valueType` classes. If the `keyType` is `String.class`, it only changes the value types by replacing each value with a new value of the specified `valueType`. If the `keyType` is not `String.class`, it creates a new map, converts both keys and values to the specified types, and populates the new map with these converted entries. The method returns the generified map.
codeFunctions: protected < K,V > Map < K,V > generifyMap (final Map < Object,Object > map,final Class < K > keyType,final Class < V > valueType) { if (keyType == String.class) { // only value type is changed, we can make value replacements for (Map.Entry < Object,Object > entry:map.entrySet ()) { Object value = entry.getValue ();Object newValue = convert (value,valueType);if (value != newValue) { entry.setValue (newValue);} } return (Map < K,V >) map;} // key is changed too, we need a new map Map < K,V > newMap = new HashMap <> (map.size ());for (Map.Entry < Object,Object > entry:map.entrySet ()) { Object key = entry.getKey ();Object newKey = convert (key,keyType);Object value = entry.getValue ();Object newValue = convert (value,valueType);newMap.put ((K) newKey,(V) newValue);} return newMap;}

originalComment: Compares two column descriptors.Identity columns should be the first on the list.Each group then will be sorted by column name.
codeComment: This method overrides the `compareTo` method to compare `DbEntityColumnDescriptor` objects. It first checks if the `isId` fields of the two objects are different. If they are, it returns -1 if the current object's `isId` is true (indicating IDs should come first), otherwise it returns 1. If the `isId` fields are the same, it compares the `columnName` fields of the two objects and returns the result of that comparison.
codeFunctions: @ Override public int compareTo (final Object o) { DbEntityColumnDescriptor that = (DbEntityColumnDescriptor) o;if (this.isId != that.isId) { return this.isId?- 1:1;// IDs should be the first in the array } return this.columnName.compareTo (that.columnName);}

originalComment: Adds default header to all requests.

originalComment: Sends new request as a browser.Before sending all browser cookies are added to the request.After sending the cookies are read from the response.Moreover status codes 301 and 302 are automatically handled.Returns very last response.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `sendRequest` method processes an `HttpRequest` object and handles various HTTP response statuses, including redirects. It measures the elapsed time for the request, adds default headers and cookies to the request, and sends the request. If exceptions occur during the request and `catchTransportExceptions` is true, it catches them and sets a 503 status code with a "Service unavailable" message. The method reads cookies from the response and checks the status code to handle redirects (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) by updating the request path and method as necessary. The process repeats until a non-redirect status code is received, and finally, it returns the `HttpResponse` object.
codeFunctions: public HttpResponse sendRequest (HttpRequest httpRequest) { elapsedTime = System.currentTimeMillis ();// send request httpRequest.followRedirects (false);while (true) { this.httpRequest = httpRequest;HttpResponse previousResponse = this.httpResponse;this.httpResponse = null;addDefaultHeaders (httpRequest);addCookies (httpRequest);// send request if (catchTransportExceptions) { try { this.httpResponse = _sendRequest (httpRequest,previousResponse);} catch (HttpException httpException) { httpResponse = new HttpResponse ();httpResponse.assignHttpRequest (httpRequest);httpResponse.statusCode (503);httpResponse.statusPhrase ("Service unavailable. " + ExceptionUtil.message (httpException));} } else { this.httpResponse = _sendRequest (httpRequest,previousResponse);} readCookies (httpResponse);int statusCode = httpResponse.statusCode ();// 301: moved permanently if (statusCode == 301) { String newPath = httpResponse.location ();if (newPath == null) { break;} httpRequest = HttpRequest.get (newPath);continue;} // 302: redirect, 303: see other if (statusCode == 302 || statusCode == 303) { String newPath = httpResponse.location ();if (newPath == null) { break;} httpRequest = HttpRequest.get (newPath);continue;} // 307: temporary redirect, 308: permanent redirect if (statusCode == 307 || statusCode == 308) { String newPath = httpResponse.location ();if (newPath == null) { break;} String originalMethod = httpRequest.method ();httpRequest = new HttpRequest ().method (originalMethod).set (newPath);continue;} break;} elapsedTime = System.currentTimeMillis () - elapsedTime;return this.httpResponse;}

originalComment: Opens connection and sends a response.
codeComment: Summary: The method `_sendRequest` sends an HTTP request using the provided `HttpRequest` object. It checks if the connection should be kept alive based on the `keepAlive` flag. If `keepAlive` is false, it opens a new connection using the `httpConnectionProvider`. If `keepAlive` is true and there is no previous response, it opens a new connection with keep-alive enabled. If there is a previous response, it uses the `keepAlive` method of the `HttpRequest` object to maintain the connection. Finally, it sends the HTTP request and returns the response.
codeFunctions: protected HttpResponse _sendRequest (final HttpRequest httpRequest,final HttpResponse previouseResponse) { if (!keepAlive) { httpRequest.open (httpConnectionProvider);} else { // keeping alive if (previouseResponse == null) { httpRequest.open (httpConnectionProvider).connectionKeepAlive (true);} else { httpRequest.keepAlive (previouseResponse,true);} } return httpRequest.send ();}

originalComment: Add default headers to the request.If request already has a header set default header will be ignored.
codeComment: The method `addDefaultHeaders` takes an `HttpRequest` object as a parameter. It iterates over a collection of default headers stored in `defaultHeaders`. For each header entry, it checks if the header name is not already present in the `httpRequest.headers`. If the header is not present, it adds the header name and its corresponding value to the `httpRequest.headers`.
codeFunctions: protected void addDefaultHeaders (final HttpRequest httpRequest) { for (Map.Entry < String,String > entry:defaultHeaders.entries ()) { String name = entry.getKey ();if (!httpRequest.headers.contains (name)) { httpRequest.headers.add (name,entry.getValue ());} } }

originalComment: Reads cookies from response and adds to cookies list.
codeComment: Summary: The `readCookies` method takes an `HttpResponse` object as a parameter, retrieves an array of `Cookie` objects from it, and iterates through each cookie. For each cookie, it adds the cookie to a `cookies` collection using the cookie's name as the key.
codeFunctions: protected void readCookies (final HttpResponse httpResponse) { Cookie [ ] newCookies = httpResponse.cookies ();for (Cookie cookie:newCookies) { cookies.add (cookie.getName (),cookie);} }

originalComment: Add cookies to the request.
codeComment: Summary: The `addCookies` method takes an `HttpRequest` object as a parameter. It initializes an empty list of `Cookie` objects. If the `cookies` map is not empty, it iterates over each entry in the map, adding the `Cookie` values to the `cookiesList`. Finally, it sets the cookies of the `httpRequest` object to the array representation of `cookiesList`.
codeFunctions: protected void addCookies (final HttpRequest httpRequest) { // prepare all cookies List < Cookie > cookiesList = new ArrayList <> ();if (!cookies.isEmpty ()) { for (Map.Entry < String,Cookie > cookieEntry:cookies) { cookiesList.add (cookieEntry.getValue ());} httpRequest.cookies (cookiesList.toArray (new Cookie [ 0 ]));} }

originalComment: Prepares message and sends it.Returns Message ID of sent email.
codeComment: The `sendMail` method takes an `Email` object as input, attempts to create a `MimeMessage` from it, and then sends this message to all specified recipients using a mail service. If the message is sent successfully, it returns the message ID. If any `MessagingException` occurs during the process, it throws a `MailException` with a descriptive error message.
codeFunctions: public String sendMail (final Email email) { try { final MimeMessage msg = createMessage (email);getService ().sendMessage (msg,msg.getAllRecipients ());return msg.getMessageID ();} catch (final MessagingException msgexc) { throw new MailException ("Failed to send email: " + email,msgexc);} }

originalComment: Sets subject in msgToSet from subject in emailWithData.
codeComment: The method `setSubject` sets the subject of a `MimeMessage` object using the subject and subject encoding from an `Email` object. If the subject encoding is specified in the `Email` object, it uses that encoding; otherwise, it sets the subject without specifying the encoding.
codeFunctions: private void setSubject (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { if (emailWithData.subjectEncoding () != null) { msgToSet.setSubject (emailWithData.subject (),emailWithData.subjectEncoding ());} else { msgToSet.setSubject (emailWithData.subject ());} }

originalComment: Sets sent date in msgToSet with sent date from emailWithData.
codeComment: Summary: The method `setSentDate` sets the sent date for a `MimeMessage` object. It retrieves the sent date from an `Email` object. If the date is not available (i.e., `null`), it uses the current date and time. The method then sets this date on the `MimeMessage` object.
codeFunctions: private void setSentDate (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { Date date = emailWithData.sentDate ();if (date == null) { date = new Date ();} msgToSet.setSentDate (date);}

originalComment: Sets headers in msgToSet with headers from emailWithData.
codeComment: The method `setHeaders` takes an `Email` object containing data and a `MimeMessage` object. It retrieves the headers from the `Email` object and sets them in the `MimeMessage` object. If the headers map is not null, it iterates through each entry in the map and sets the header key-value pairs in the `MimeMessage`. This method throws a `MessagingException` if an error occurs during the process.
codeFunctions: private void setHeaders (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { final Map < String,String > headers = emailWithData.headers ();if (headers != null) { for (final Map.Entry < String,String > entry:headers.entrySet ()) { msgToSet.setHeader (entry.getKey (),entry.getValue ());} } }

originalComment: Sets FROM REPLY - TO and recipients.
codeComment: Summary: The `setPeople` method configures the sender and reply-to addresses of a `MimeMessage` object using data from an `Email` object. It sets the sender using the `from()` method of `Email` and converts it to an `InternetAddress`. It sets the reply-to addresses by converting the list of `EmailAddress` objects from `Email` to an array of `InternetAddress` objects. Additionally, it calls the `setRecipients` method to set the recipients of the message.
codeFunctions: private void setPeople (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { msgToSet.setFrom (emailWithData.from ().toInternetAddress ());msgToSet.setReplyTo (EmailAddress.convert (emailWithData.replyTo ()));setRecipients (emailWithData,msgToSet);}

originalComment: Sets TO CC and BCC in msgToSet with TO CC and BCC from emailWithData.
codeComment: The method `setRecipients` takes an `Email` object containing recipient data and a `MimeMessage` object. It converts the recipient email addresses from the `Email` object into `InternetAddress` arrays for TO, CC, and BCC recipients. If there are any addresses in these arrays, it sets them as the respective recipients in the `MimeMessage` object. This method handles setting multiple types of recipients and ensures that only non-empty recipient lists are processed.
codeFunctions: private void setRecipients (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { // TO final InternetAddress [ ] to = EmailAddress.convert (emailWithData.to ());if (to.length > 0) { msgToSet.setRecipients (RecipientType.TO,to);} // CC final InternetAddress [ ] cc = EmailAddress.convert (emailWithData.cc ());if (cc.length > 0) { msgToSet.setRecipients (RecipientType.CC,cc);} // BCC final InternetAddress [ ] bcc = EmailAddress.convert (emailWithData.bcc ());if (bcc.length > 0) { msgToSet.setRecipients (RecipientType.BCC,bcc);} }

originalComment: Adds message data and attachments.
codeComment: The method `addBodyData` takes an `Email` object containing email data and a `MimeMessage` object to which the email data will be set. It processes the email's messages and attachments, and sets the content of the `MimeMessage` accordingly. If there are no attachments and only one message, it directly sets the content of the `MimeMessage` to that single message. Otherwise, it creates a `MimeMultipart` object, adds a base body part, and iterates through the email messages to add each as a body part to an alternative `MimeMultipart`. It then adds any attachments to the main `MimeMultipart` and sets this as the content of the `MimeMessage`.
codeFunctions: private void addBodyData (final Email emailWithData,final MimeMessage msgToSet) throws MessagingException { final List < EmailMessage > messages = emailWithData.messages ();final int totalMessages = messages.size ();// Need to use new list since filterEmbeddedAttachments(List) removes attachments from the source List final List < EmailAttachment <?extends DataSource > > attachments = new ArrayList <> (emailWithData.attachments ());if (attachments.isEmpty () && totalMessages == 1) { // special case: no attachments and just one content setContent (messages.get (0),msgToSet);} else { final MimeMultipart multipart = new MimeMultipart ();final MimeMultipart msgMultipart = new MimeMultipart (ALTERNATIVE);multipart.addBodyPart (getBaseBodyPart (msgMultipart));for (final EmailMessage emailMessage:messages) { msgMultipart.addBodyPart (getBodyPart (emailMessage,attachments));} addAnyAttachments (attachments,multipart);msgToSet.setContent (multipart);} }

originalComment: Sets emailWithData content into msgToSet.
codeComment: Summary: The `setContent` method sets the content of a given `Part` object using the content, MIME type, and encoding from an `EmailMessage` object. It throws a `MessagingException` if an error occurs during the process.
codeFunctions: private void setContent (final EmailMessage emailWithData,final Part partToSet) throws MessagingException { partToSet.setContent (emailWithData.getContent (),emailWithData.getMimeType () + CHARSET + emailWithData.getEncoding ());}

originalComment: Creates attachment body part.Handles regular and inline attachments.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `createAttachmentBodyPart` method constructs a `MimeBodyPart` for an email attachment. It sets the file name using the encoded name from the attachment if available, assigns a `DataHandler` with the attachment's data source, and optionally sets a content ID and disposition if the attachment is inline. The method returns the configured `MimeBodyPart`.
codeFunctions: protected MimeBodyPart createAttachmentBodyPart (final EmailAttachment <?extends DataSource > attachment) throws MessagingException { final MimeBodyPart part = new MimeBodyPart ();final String attachmentName = attachment.getEncodedName ();if (attachmentName != null) { part.setFileName (attachmentName);} part.setDataHandler (new DataHandler (attachment.getDataSource ()));if (attachment.getContentId () != null) { part.setContentID (StringPool.LEFT_CHEV + attachment.getContentId () + StringPool.RIGHT_CHEV);} if (attachment.isInline ()) { part.setDisposition (INLINE);} return part;}

originalComment: Strips content type information from requests data header.
codeComment: The method `getContentType` extracts the content type from a given data header string. It searches for the substring "Content-Type:" within the `dataHeader`. If the substring is found, it returns the trimmed content type value that follows "Content-Type:". If the substring is not found, it returns an empty string.
codeFunctions: private String getContentType (final String dataHeader) { String token = "Content-Type:";int start = dataHeader.indexOf (token);if (start == - 1) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} start += token.length ();return dataHeader.substring (start).trim ();}

originalComment: Stores result set.
codeComment: Summary: The method `saveResultSet` takes a `ResultSet` object as a parameter. It checks if the `resultSets` collection is null, and if so, initializes it as a new `HashSet`. Then, it adds the provided `ResultSet` to the `resultSets` collection.

originalComment: Closes all result sets created by this query.Query remains active.
codeComment: Summary: The method `closeAllResultSets` attempts to close all associated `ResultSet` objects by calling `closeQueryResultSets`. If an `SQLException` is thrown during this process, it catches the exception and rethrows it as a `DbSqlException` with a descriptive message. Finally, it returns the current instance (`_this()`).
codeFunctions: public Q closeAllResultSets () { final SQLException sex = closeQueryResultSets ();if (sex != null) { throw new DbSqlException ("Close associated ResultSets error",sex);} return _this ();}

originalComment: Closes all assigned result sets and then closes the query.Query becomes closed.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `closeQuery` method is designed to close query resources and handle any `SQLException` that might occur during the process. It first attempts to close any `ResultSet` objects by calling `closeQueryResultSets()`. If a `statement` object is not null, it tries to close the `statement`. If an `SQLException` occurs while closing the `statement`, it checks if an `SQLException` from `closeQueryResultSets()` already exists. If not, it sets the new exception; otherwise, it chains the new exception to the existing one using `setNextException()`. After attempting to close the `statement`, it sets the `statement` reference to null. Finally, it sets the `query` reference to null and changes the `queryState` to `CLOSED`. The method returns any `SQLException` that occurred during the process.
codeFunctions: protected SQLException closeQuery () { SQLException sqlException = closeQueryResultSets ();if (statement != null) { try { statement.close ();} catch (SQLException sex) { if (sqlException == null) { sqlException = sex;} else { sqlException.setNextException (sex);} } statement = null;} query = null;queryState = CLOSED;return sqlException;}

originalComment: Closes the query and all created results sets and detaches itself from the session.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `close` method is an overridden function that handles the closing of a query and manages related resources. It first attempts to close the query and captures any `SQLException` that might occur. It then sets the `connection` variable to `null` and detaches the query from the session if the session is not `null`. If an `SQLException` was caught during the query closure, it throws a `DbSqlException` with a message "Close query error" and the original `SQLException` as the cause.
codeFunctions: @ Override @ SuppressWarnings ({ "ClassReferencesSubclass" }) public void close () { final SQLException sqlException = closeQuery ();connection = null;if (this.session != null) { this.session.detachQuery (this);} if (sqlException != null) { throw new DbSqlException ("Close query error",sqlException);} }

originalComment: Gives the JDBC driver a hint as to the number of rows that should be fetched from the database when more rows are needed.The number of rows specified affects only result sets created using this statement.If the value specified is zero then the hint is ignored.The default value is zero.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `setFetchSize` method sets the number of rows that should be fetched from the database in one round trip. It first checks if the object is not closed, then updates the `fetchSize` field. If a `statement` object is available, it attempts to set the fetch size on the statement. If an `SQLException` occurs during this process, it throws a `DbSqlException` with an appropriate error message. Finally, it returns the current object (`_this()`).
codeFunctions: public Q setFetchSize (final int rows) { checkNotClosed ();this.fetchSize = rows;if (statement != null) { try { statement.setFetchSize (fetchSize);} catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"Unable to set fetch size: " + fetchSize,sex);} } return _this ();}

originalComment: Sets the limit for the maximum number of rows that any ResultSet object can contain to the given number.If the limit is exceeded the excess rows are silently dropped.Zero means there is no limit.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `setMaxRows` method sets the maximum number of rows that a `Q` object can return. It first checks if the object is not closed, then updates the `maxRows` field. If a `statement` object is associated with the `Q` object, it attempts to set the maximum number of rows on the `statement` as well. If an `SQLException` occurs during this process, it throws a `DbSqlException` with an appropriate error message. Finally, it returns the current instance of the `Q` object.
codeFunctions: public Q setMaxRows (final int maxRows) { checkNotClosed ();this.maxRows = maxRows;if (statement != null) { try { statement.setMaxRows (maxRows);} catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"Unable to set max rows: " + maxRows,sex);} } return _this ();}

originalComment: Executes UPDATE INSERT or DELETE queries and optionally closes the query.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `executeUpdate` method is a protected method that executes an SQL update query. It measures the execution time, logs the query if debugging is enabled, and handles exceptions by throwing a `DbSqlException`. The method uses either a `Statement` or a `PreparedStatement` based on which is available. If `generatedColumns` are specified, it handles the generation of keys accordingly. After executing the update, it optionally closes the query resources and logs the elapsed execution time. The method returns the result of the update operation.
codeFunctions: protected int executeUpdate (final boolean closeQuery) { start = System.currentTimeMillis ();init ();final int result;if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("Executing update: " + getQueryString ());} try { if (preparedStatement == null) { if (generatedColumns != null) { if (generatedColumns.length == 0) { result = statement.executeUpdate (query.sql,Statement.RETURN_GENERATED_KEYS);} else { result = statement.executeUpdate (query.sql,generatedColumns);} } else { result = statement.executeUpdate (query.sql);} } else { result = preparedStatement.executeUpdate ();} } catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"Query execution failed",sex);} if (closeQuery) { close ();} elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis () - start;if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("execution time: " + elapsed + "ms");} return result;}

originalComment: Executes count queries and optionally closes query afterwards.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `executeCount` method is a protected method that executes a SQL count query and returns the result as a `long`. It measures the execution time of the query and logs it if debugging is enabled. The method handles both `Statement` and `PreparedStatement` objects. If an exception occurs during the execution, it throws a `DbSqlException`. After executing the query, it closes the `ResultSet` and optionally closes the current object if the `close` parameter is `true`.
codeFunctions: protected long executeCount (final boolean close) { start = System.currentTimeMillis ();init ();ResultSet rs = null;if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("Executing prepared count: " + getQueryString ());} try { if (preparedStatement == null) { rs = statement.executeQuery (query.sql);} else { rs = preparedStatement.executeQuery ();} final long firstLong = DbUtil.getFirstLong (rs);elapsed = System.currentTimeMillis () - start;if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("execution time: " + elapsed + "ms");} return firstLong;} catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"Count query failed",sex);} finally { DbUtil.close (rs);if (close) { close ();} } }

originalComment: Returns generated columns.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `getGeneratedColumns` method first checks if the object is initialized. It then verifies if `generatedColumns` is null, throwing a `DbSqlException` if it is. The method attempts to retrieve generated keys from the `statement` object, catching any `SQLException` and rethrowing it as a `DbSqlException`. If successful, it saves the `ResultSet` and increments the `totalOpenResultSetCount` before returning the `ResultSet`.
codeFunctions: public ResultSet getGeneratedColumns () { checkInitialized ();if (generatedColumns == null) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"No column is specified as auto-generated");} final ResultSet rs;try { rs = statement.getGeneratedKeys ();} catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbSqlException (this,"No generated keys",sex);} saveResultSet (rs);totalOpenResultSetCount ++;return rs;}

originalComment: Returns query SQL string.For prepared statements returned sql string with quick - and - dirty replaced values.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `getQueryString` method returns a query string based on the available statement objects and debug mode. If `debug` is true and `callableStatement` is not null, it checks if `callableStatement` is an instance of `LoggableCallableStatement` and returns its query string. If `preparedStatement` is not null, it checks if it is an instance of `LoggablePreparedStatement` and returns its query string. If `query` is not null, it returns `query.sql`. If none of the above conditions are met, it returns `sqlString`.
codeFunctions: public String getQueryString () { if (debug) { if ((callableStatement != null)) { if (preparedStatement instanceof LoggableCallableStatement) { return ((LoggableCallableStatement) callableStatement).getQueryString ();} } if (preparedStatement != null) { if (preparedStatement instanceof LoggablePreparedStatement) { return ((LoggablePreparedStatement) preparedStatement).getQueryString ();} } } if (query != null) { return query.sql;} return sqlString;}

originalComment: Creates a proxy of given target and the aspect.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `proxyOf` method creates a proxy instance for a given target object using a specified aspect class. It first attempts to instantiate the aspect class, passing the target object to its constructor. If instantiation fails, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. If successful, it returns a new proxy instance that wraps the target object, using the aspect for additional behavior, and implements the same interfaces as the target object.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public static < T > T proxyOf (final T target,final Class <?extends Aspect > aspectClass) { final Aspect aspect;try { aspect = ClassUtil.newInstance (aspectClass,target);} catch (Exception e) { throw new IllegalArgumentException ("Can't create new instance of aspect class",e);} return (T) newProxyInstance (target.getClass ().getClassLoader (),aspect,target.getClass ().getInterfaces ());}

originalComment: Returns a collection containing all elements of the iterator.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `collectionOf` takes an `Iterator` of a generic type `T` as input and returns a `Collection` (specifically, an `ArrayList`) containing all the elements that the iterator iterates over. It initializes an empty `ArrayList`, then iterates through the provided iterator, adding each element to the list. Finally, it returns the populated list.
codeFunctions: public static < T > Collection < T > collectionOf (final Iterator <?extends T > iterator) { final List < T > list = new ArrayList <> ();while (iterator.hasNext ()) { list.add (iterator.next ());} return list;}

originalComment: Converts iterator to a stream.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `streamOf` takes an `Iterator<T>` as input and returns a `Stream<T>`. It achieves this by converting the iterator into an `Iterable<T>` using a lambda expression, then creating a spliterator from this iterable, and finally generating a stream from the spliterator with the parallelism flag set to `false`.
codeFunctions: public static < T > Stream < T > streamOf (final Iterator < T > iterator) { return StreamSupport.stream (((Iterable < T >) () -> iterator).spliterator (),false);}

originalComment: Compares two objects starting with first comparator;if they are equals proceeds to the next comparator and so on.
codeComment: This method overrides the `compare` method from the `Comparator` interface. It takes two objects of type `T` as input and compares them using a list of comparators. The method iterates through each comparator in the `comparators` list, applying the `compare` method to the two input objects. If any comparator returns a non-zero result, indicating that the objects are not equal according to that comparator, the method immediately returns that result. If all comparators return zero, indicating that the objects are equal according to all comparators, the method returns 0.
codeFunctions: @ Override public int compare (final T o1,final T o2) { for (Comparator < T > comparator:comparators) { int result = comparator.compare (o1,o2);if (result != 0) { return result;} } return 0;}

originalComment: Specifies default wiring mode.
codeComment: Summary: The `setDefaultWiringMode` method sets the default wiring mode for a `PetiteConfig` object. It accepts a `WiringMode` parameter and throws a `PetiteException` if the provided mode is `null` or `WiringMode.DEFAULT`. If the input is valid, it assigns the mode to the `defaultWiringMode` field and returns the current `PetiteConfig` instance.
codeFunctions: public PetiteConfig setDefaultWiringMode (final WiringMode defaultWiringMode) { if ((defaultWiringMode == null) || (defaultWiringMode == WiringMode.DEFAULT)) { throw new PetiteException ("Invalid default wiring mode: " + defaultWiringMode);} this.defaultWiringMode = defaultWiringMode;return this;}

originalComment: Prints error message if level is enabled.
codeComment: This method, `print`, logs a message with a specified log level and an optional throwable. It first checks if the logging for the given level is enabled. If not, it returns immediately. If logging is enabled, it constructs a log message that includes the elapsed time, log level, caller class, and the provided message. This constructed message is then printed to the standard output. If a throwable is provided, its stack trace is also printed to the standard output.
codeFunctions: protected void print (final Level level,final String message,final Throwable throwable) { if (!isEnabled (level)) { return;} StringBuilder msg = new StringBuilder ().append (slf.getElapsedTime ()).append (' ').append (' ').append (level).append (' ').append (' ').append (getCallerClass ()).append (' ').append (' ').append (' ').append (message);System.out.println (msg.toString ());if (throwable != null) { throwable.printStackTrace (System.out);} }

originalComment: Returns called class.
codeComment: This method, `getCallerClass`, retrieves information about the caller class by creating an exception and examining its stack trace. It iterates through the stack trace elements, skipping entries related to `SimpleLoggerProvider`, `SimpleLogger`, and `Logger` classes. For the first stack trace element that does not match these classes, it returns a string containing the shortened class name, method name, and line number. If no such element is found, it returns "N/A".
codeFunctions: protected String getCallerClass () { Exception exception = new Exception ();StackTraceElement [ ] stackTrace = exception.getStackTrace ();for (StackTraceElement stackTraceElement:stackTrace) { String className = stackTraceElement.getClassName ();if (className.equals (SimpleLoggerProvider.class.getName ())) { continue;} if (className.equals (SimpleLogger.class.getName ())) { continue;} if (className.equals (Logger.class.getName ())) { continue;} return shortenClassName (className) + ' ' + stackTraceElement.getMethodName () + ' ' + stackTraceElement.getLineNumber ();} return "N/A";}

### Summary:
The `shortenClassName` method takes a `String` representing a class name and shortens it by removing all characters before the last space, including the space itself, while preserving the part of the string after the last space. If there is no space in the input string, it returns the original string unchanged. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the shortened class name.
codeFunctions: protected String shortenClassName (final String className) { int lastDotIndex = className.lastIndexOf (' ');if (lastDotIndex == - 1) { return className;} StringBuilder shortClassName = new StringBuilder (className.length ());int start = 0;while (true) { shortClassName.append (className.charAt (start));int next = className.indexOf (' ',start);if (next == lastDotIndex) { break;} start = next + 1;shortClassName.append (' ');} shortClassName.append (className.substring (lastDotIndex));return shortClassName.toString ();}

### Summary:
The method `cloneViaSerialization` is a generic method that clones an object of type `T` by serializing it to a byte array and then deserializing it back to an object. It uses `FastByteArrayOutputStream` and `ObjectOutputStream` to serialize the object, and `ObjectInputStream` to deserialize it. codeFunctions: public static < T extends Serializable > T cloneViaSerialization (final T obj) throws IOException,ClassNotFoundException { FastByteArrayOutputStream bos = new FastByteArrayOutputStream ();ObjectOutputStream out = null;ObjectInputStream in = null;Object objCopy = null;try { out = new ObjectOutputStream (bos);out.writeObject (obj);out.flush ();byte [ ] bytes = bos.toByteArray ();in = new ObjectInputStream (new ByteArrayInputStream (bytes));objCopy = in.readObject ();} finally { StreamUtil.close (out);StreamUtil.close (in);} return (T) objCopy;}

originalComment: Resolved mapped type names for each type.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `resolveMappedTypesTableNames` takes an array of `Class` objects as input and returns a 2D array of `String` objects. It first checks if `cachedMappedNames` is `null`. If it is, it initializes a 2D array `names` with the same length as the input array. It then iterates over each `Class` object in the input array. For each non-null `Class`, it retrieves the corresponding `DbEntityDescriptor` from `cachedDbEntityDescriptors`. If the `DbEntityDescriptor` is not `null`, it gets the mapped types from the descriptor. If the mapped types are not `null`, it calls `createTypesTableNames` with the mapped types to generate table names and stores them in the `names` array. After processing all classes, it assigns the `names` array to `cachedMappedNames` and returns it. If `cachedMappedNames` is not `null`, it simply returns the cached value.
codeFunctions: protected String [ ] [ ] resolveMappedTypesTableNames (final Class [ ] types) { if (cachedMappedNames == null) { String [ ] [ ] names = new String [ types.length ] [  ];for (int i = 0;i < types.length;i ++) { Class type = types [ i ];if (type != null) { DbEntityDescriptor ded = cachedDbEntityDescriptors [ i ];if (ded != null) { Class [ ] mappedTypes = ded.getMappedTypes ();if (mappedTypes != null) { names [ i ] = createTypesTableNames (mappedTypes);} } } } cachedMappedNames = names;} return cachedMappedNames;}

originalComment: Creates table names for given types.
codeComment: The method `createTypesTableNames` takes an array of `Class` objects as input and returns an array of `String` objects. It iterates over each `Class` in the input array. For each `Class`, it checks if the `Class` is `null`. If it is, the corresponding entry in the result array is set to `null`. If the `Class` is not `null`, it looks up the `DbEntityDescriptor` for that `Class` using `dbEntityManager.lookupType`. If a `DbEntityDescriptor` is found, it retrieves the table name from the descriptor, converts it to uppercase, and stores it in the result array. Finally, the method returns the array of table names.
codeFunctions: protected String [ ] createTypesTableNames (final Class [ ] types) { String [ ] names = new String [ types.length ];for (int i = 0;i < types.length;i ++) { if (types [ i ] == null) { names [ i ] = null;continue;} DbEntityDescriptor ded = dbEntityManager.lookupType (types [ i ]);if (ded != null) { String tableName = ded.getTableName ();tableName = tableName.toUpperCase ();names [ i ] = tableName;} } return names;}

originalComment: Reads column value from result set.Since this method may be called more then once for the same column it caches column values.
codeComment: This method, `readColumnValue`, reads a value from a specified column in a database result set and converts it to the desired destination type. It first checks if the column index has changed since the last read. If it has, it attempts to retrieve the value using an appropriate `SqlType` instance if provided, or by looking up a suitable type based on the destination type. If no suitable `SqlType` is found, it retrieves the value as an `Object` and then converts it to the destination type using a `TypeConverterManager`. If an `SQLException` occurs during this process, it throws a `DbOomException`. The method caches the column index and value for future calls.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ({ "unchecked" }) protected Object readColumnValue (final int colNdx,final Class destinationType,final Class <?extends SqlType > sqlTypeClass,final int columnDbSqlType) { if (colNdx != cachedColumnNdx) { try { SqlType sqlType;if (sqlTypeClass != null) { sqlType = SqlTypeManager.get ().lookupSqlType (sqlTypeClass);} else { sqlType = SqlTypeManager.get ().lookup (destinationType);} if (sqlType != null) { cachedColumnValue = sqlType.readValue (resultSet,colNdx + 1,destinationType,columnDbSqlType);} else { cachedColumnValue = resultSet.getObject (colNdx + 1);cachedColumnValue = TypeConverterManager.get ().convertType (cachedColumnValue,destinationType);} } catch (SQLException sex) { throw new DbOomException (dbOomQuery,"Invalid value for column #" + (colNdx + 1),sex);} cachedColumnNdx = colNdx;} return cachedColumnValue;}

originalComment: Caches returned entities.Replaces new instances with existing ones.
codeComment: The method `cacheResultSetEntities` takes an array of objects as input and caches them in a `HashMap` called `entitiesCache`. If `entitiesCache` is null, it initializes it. For each object in the input array, it checks if the object is null and skips it if true. It then retrieves a `DbEntityDescriptor` from an array `cachedDbEntityDescriptors` for the current index. If the `DbEntityDescriptor` is null, it skips the object. It calculates a key for the object: if the `DbEntityDescriptor` has an ID column, it uses the value of that column as the key; otherwise, it uses the object itself as the key. It checks if the object is already in the cache using the calculated key. If not, it adds the object to the cache. If the object is already in the cache, it replaces the object in the input array with the cached object.
codeFunctions: protected void cacheResultSetEntities (final Object [ ] result) { if (entitiesCache == null) { entitiesCache = new HashMap <> ();} for (int i = 0;i < result.length;i ++) { Object object = result [ i ];if (object == null) { continue;} DbEntityDescriptor ded = cachedDbEntityDescriptors [ i ];if (ded == null) { // not a type, continue continue;} // calculate key Object key;if (ded.hasIdColumn ()) { //noinspection unchecked key = ded.getKeyValue (object);} else { key = object;} Object cachedObject = entitiesCache.get (key);if (cachedObject == null) { // object is not in the cache, add it entitiesCache.put (key,object);} else { // object is in the cache, replace it result [ i ] = cachedObject;} } }

originalComment: Resolves all providers in the class
codeComment: The method `resolve` takes a `Class` type and a `String` name as parameters. It retrieves the `ClassDescriptor` for the given class using `ClassIntrospector`. It then iterates over all method descriptors of the class. For each method, it checks if the method is annotated with `PetiteProvider`. If not, it skips to the next method. If the method is annotated, it retrieves the provider name from the annotation; if the name is blank, it defaults to the method name, removing the "Provider" suffix if present. It then creates a `ProviderDefinition` object, considering whether the method is static or not, and adds it to a list. Finally, it converts the list to an array of `ProviderDefinition` objects and returns it. If no provider definitions are found, it returns an empty array.
codeFunctions: public ProviderDefinition [ ] resolve (final Class type,final String name) { ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (type);MethodDescriptor [ ] methods = cd.getAllMethodDescriptors ();List < ProviderDefinition > list = new ArrayList <> ();for (MethodDescriptor methodDescriptor:methods) { Method method = methodDescriptor.getMethod ();PetiteProvider petiteProvider = method.getAnnotation (PetiteProvider.class);if (petiteProvider == null) { continue;} String providerName = petiteProvider.value ();if (StringUtil.isBlank (providerName)) { // default provider name providerName = method.getName ();if (providerName.endsWith ("Provider")) { providerName = StringUtil.substring (providerName,0,- 8);} } ProviderDefinition providerDefinition;if (Modifier.isStatic (method.getModifiers ())) { providerDefinition = new ProviderDefinition (providerName,method);} else { providerDefinition = new ProviderDefinition (providerName,name,method);} list.add (providerDefinition);} ProviderDefinition [ ] providers;if (list.isEmpty ()) { providers = ProviderDefinition.EMPTY;} else { providers = list.toArray (new ProviderDefinition [ 0 ]);} return providers;}
