codeFunctions: public Props load (final Map <?,?> p) { for (final Map.Entry <?,?> entry:p.entrySet ()) { final String name = entry.getKey ().toString ();final Object value = entry.getValue ();if (value == null) { continue;} data.putBaseProperty (name,value.toString (),false);} return this;}

originalComment: Loads base properties from java Map using provided prefix.Null values are ignored.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `load` method takes a `Map` and a `String` prefix as parameters. It iterates over each entry in the map, constructs a new key by appending the entry's key to the prefix with a space in between, and adds this new key-value pair to a `data` object's base properties. If the value is `null`, it skips that entry. The method returns the current instance (`this`). The `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")` annotation is used to suppress unchecked type warnings.
codeFunctions: @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public Props load (final Map <?,?> map,final String prefix) { String realPrefix = prefix;realPrefix += ' ';for (final Map.Entry entry:map.entrySet ()) { final String name = entry.getKey ().toString ();final Object value = entry.getValue ();if (value == null) { continue;} data.putBaseProperty (realPrefix + name,value.toString (),false);} return this;}

originalComment: Loads props and properties from the classpath.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `loadFromClasspath` method scans the default classpath for resources matching the provided patterns. For each matching resource, it checks if the resource name ends with ".properties" to determine the appropriate encoding (ISO-8859-1 for properties files, otherwise using the default encoding from `JoddCore.encoding`). It then loads the resource using the determined encoding. The method ignores exceptions during the scanning process and excludes common JAR files and all entries by default, only including those that match the specified patterns. Finally, it returns the current instance (`this`).
codeFunctions: public Props loadFromClasspath (final String ... patterns) { ClassScanner.create ().registerEntryConsumer (entryData -> { String usedEncoding = JoddCore.encoding;if (StringUtil.endsWithIgnoreCase (entryData.name (),".properties")) { usedEncoding = StringPool.ISO_8859_1;} final String encoding = usedEncoding;UncheckedException.runAndWrapException (() -> load (entryData.openInputStream (),encoding));}).includeResources (true).ignoreException (true).excludeCommonJars ().excludeAllEntries (true).includeEntries (patterns).scanDefaultClasspath ().start ();return this;}

originalComment: Adds child map to the props on given prefix.
codeComment: The method `addInnerMap` takes a prefix, a map, and a profile as parameters. It ensures the prefix ends with a dot if it doesn't already. Then, it iterates over each entry in the map, constructs a new key by concatenating the prefix with the original key, and sets the value associated with this new key in the specified profile.

originalComment: Resolves active profiles from special property.This property can be only a base property! If default active property is not defined nothing happens.Otherwise it will replace currently active profiles.
codeComment: Summary: The method `resolveActiveProfiles` sets the `activeProfiles` based on the value of `activeProfilesProp`. If `activeProfilesProp` is null, `activeProfiles` is set to null and the method returns. It retrieves the property value from `data` using `getBaseProperty`. If the property value is null or blank, `activeProfiles` is set to null. Otherwise, it splits the value by spaces into an array, trims each element, and assigns it to `activeProfiles`.
codeFunctions: protected void resolveActiveProfiles () { if (activeProfilesProp == null) { activeProfiles = null;return;} final PropsEntry pv = data.getBaseProperty (activeProfilesProp);if (pv == null) { // no active profile set as the property, exit return;} final String value = pv.getValue ();if (StringUtil.isBlank (value)) { activeProfiles = null;return;} activeProfiles = StringUtil.splitc (value,' ');StringUtil.trimAll (activeProfiles);}

codeFunctions: public String [ ] getAllProfiles () { String [ ] profiles = new String [ data.profileProperties.size () ];int index = 0;for (String profileName:data.profileProperties.keySet ()) { profiles [ index ] = profileName;index ++;} return profiles;}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `getProfilesFor` takes a wildcard string `propKeyNameWildcard` as input and returns an array of profile names. It iterates through a map of profile properties, checking each property key name against the wildcard. If a match is found, the corresponding profile name is added to a set to ensure uniqueness. Finally, the method returns the profile names as an array of strings.
codeFunctions: public String [ ] getProfilesFor (final String propKeyNameWildcard) { HashSet < String > profiles = new HashSet <> ();profile:for (Map.Entry < String,Map < String,PropsEntry > > entries:data.profileProperties.entrySet ()) { String profileName = entries.getKey ();Map < String,PropsEntry > value = entries.getValue ();for (String propKeyName:value.keySet ()) { if (Wildcard.equalsOrMatch (propKeyName,propKeyNameWildcard)) { profiles.add (profileName);continue profile;} } } return profiles.toArray (new String [ 0 ]);}

originalComment: Returns target class if proxetta applied on given class.If not returns given class as result.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `resolveTargetClass` method determines the target class from a given proxy class. It checks the proxy class's name to see if it ends with a specific suffix defined in `ProxettaNames.proxyClassNameSuffix`. If it does, the method returns the superclass of the proxy. If the name ends with another suffix defined in `ProxettaNames.wrapperClassNameSuffix`, it calls `getTargetWrapperType` to determine the target class. If neither condition is met, it returns the proxy class itself.
codeFunctions: public static Class resolveTargetClass (final Class proxy) { final String name = proxy.getName ();if (name.endsWith (ProxettaNames.proxyClassNameSuffix)) { return proxy.getSuperclass ();} if (name.endsWith (ProxettaNames.wrapperClassNameSuffix)) { return getTargetWrapperType (proxy);} return proxy;}

It attempts to retrieve a field from this class using the name specified in `ProxettaNames.wrapperTargetFieldName`. If the field is found, the method returns the type of this field. If the field does not exist, a `ProxettaException` is thrown, wrapping the original `NoSuchFieldException`.
codeFunctions: public static Class getTargetWrapperType (final Class wrapperClass) { try { final Field field = wrapperClass.getDeclaredField (ProxettaNames.wrapperTargetFieldName);return field.getType ();} catch (NoSuchFieldException nsfex) { throw new ProxettaException (nsfex);} }

originalComment: Locates property field.Field is being searched also in all superclasses of current class.
codeComment: The method `findField` searches for a `FieldDescriptor` with the specified `fieldName` within the current class and its superclasses. It first attempts to retrieve the `FieldDescriptor` from the `classDescriptor` of the current class. If the `FieldDescriptor` is not found, it iterates through all superclasses, attempting to find the `FieldDescriptor` in each superclass's `classDescriptor`. If the `FieldDescriptor` is found in any superclass, it is returned. If no `FieldDescriptor` is found after checking all superclasses, the method returns `null`.
codeFunctions: protected FieldDescriptor findField (final String fieldName) { FieldDescriptor fieldDescriptor = classDescriptor.getFieldDescriptor (fieldName,true);if (fieldDescriptor != null) { return fieldDescriptor;} // field descriptor not found in this class // try to locate it in the superclasses Class [ ] superclasses = classDescriptor.getAllSuperclasses ();for (Class superclass:superclasses) { ClassDescriptor classDescriptor = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (superclass);fieldDescriptor = classDescriptor.getFieldDescriptor (fieldName,true);if (fieldDescriptor != null) { return fieldDescriptor;} } // nothing found return null;}

originalComment: Returns property type.Raw types are detected.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `getType` method returns the type of a field or method descriptor. If the `type` is not already set, it checks for a `fieldDescriptor`, `readMethodDescriptor`, or `writeMethodDescriptor` in that order. If a `fieldDescriptor` is found, it retrieves the raw type using `getRawType()`. If a `readMethodDescriptor` is found, it uses the `getGetter` method to obtain the raw type. Similarly, if a `writeMethodDescriptor` is found, it uses the `getSetter` method to obtain the raw type. Finally, the method returns the determined `type`.
codeFunctions: public Class getType () { if (type == null) { if (fieldDescriptor != null) { type = fieldDescriptor.getRawType ();} else if (readMethodDescriptor != null) { type = getGetter (true).getGetterRawType ();//type = readMethodDescriptor.getGetterRawType(); } else if (writeMethodDescriptor != null) { type = getSetter (true).getSetterRawType ();//type = writeMethodDescriptor.getSetterRawType(); } } return type;}

originalComment: Resolves key type for given property descriptor.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `resolveKeyType` method determines the key type based on whether a getter or field descriptor is available. It first attempts to retrieve the key type from a getter if one is declared. If no getter is found or it does not provide a key type, it then checks a field descriptor for the key type. If neither source provides a key type, the method returns `null`.
codeFunctions: public Class resolveKeyType (final boolean declared) { Class keyType = null;Getter getter = getGetter (declared);if (getter != null) { keyType = getter.getGetterRawKeyComponentType ();} if (keyType == null) { FieldDescriptor fieldDescriptor = getFieldDescriptor ();if (fieldDescriptor != null) { keyType = fieldDescriptor.getRawKeyComponentType ();} } return keyType;}

codeFunctions: public Class resolveComponentType (final boolean declared) { Class componentType = null;Getter getter = getGetter (declared);if (getter != null) { componentType = getter.getGetterRawComponentType ();} if (componentType == null) { FieldDescriptor fieldDescriptor = getFieldDescriptor ();if (fieldDescriptor != null) { componentType = fieldDescriptor.getRawComponentType ();} } return componentType;}

originalComment: Creates a JSON response from an exception.Response body will have information about the exception and response status will be set to 500.

### Summary:
The method `of` takes an `Exception` as input and constructs a `JsonResult` object containing detailed error information. It creates a `HashMap` to store error details, including the exception message, error class name, and cause class name (if available). It also collects the stack trace elements into an `ArrayList` and adds them to the `HashMap`. The `HashMap` is then serialized into a JSON string using `JsonSerializer`, and a `JsonResult` object is returned with the JSON string and an HTTP status of 500 (Internal Server Error).
codeFunctions: public static JsonResult of (final Exception exception) { final HashMap < String,Object > errorMap = new HashMap <> ();errorMap.put ("message",ExceptionUtil.message (exception));errorMap.put ("error",exception.getClass ().getName ());errorMap.put ("cause",exception.getCause () != null?exception.getCause ().getClass ().getName ():null);final ArrayList < String > details = new ArrayList <> ();final StackTraceElement [ ] ste = ExceptionUtil.getStackTrace (exception,null,null);for (StackTraceElement stackTraceElement:ste) { details.add (stackTraceElement.toString ());} errorMap.put ("details",details);final String json = JsonSerializer.create ().deep (true).serialize (errorMap);return new JsonResult (json).status (HttpStatus.error500 ().internalError ());}

originalComment: Resolves HTTP method name from method name.If method name or first camel - case word of a method equals to a HTTP method it will be used as that HTTP methods.
codeComment: The method `resolveHttpMethodFromMethodName` takes a `String` parameter `methodName` and attempts to determine an HTTP method from the beginning of the method name. It iterates through the characters of `methodName` until it finds an uppercase letter, indicating the start of the HTTP method name. It then converts this substring to uppercase and checks if it matches any of the names in the `HttpMethod` enum. If a match is found, it returns the name of the HTTP method; otherwise, it returns `null`.
codeFunctions: protected String resolveHttpMethodFromMethodName (final String methodName) { int i = 0;while (i < methodName.length ()) { if (CharUtil.isUppercaseAlpha (methodName.charAt (i))) { break;} i ++;} final String name = methodName.substring (0,i).toUpperCase ();for (final HttpMethod httpMethod:HttpMethod.values ()) { if (httpMethod.equalsName (name)) { return httpMethod.name ();} } return null;}

originalComment: Internal matching recursive function.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `match` method is a recursive function designed to determine if a given `string` matches a specified `pattern`. The pattern can include wildcard characters, represented by spaces in this context. Here's a breakdown of the method:

1. **Initial Checks**:
   - If the pattern length is 1 and the character is a space, it immediately returns `true` as a space acts as a wildcard matching any string.
   - It calculates the lengths of both the `string` and `pattern`.

2. **Loop Through Characters**:
   - The method uses a `while` loop to iterate through both the `string` and `pattern`.
   - It checks if the end of the `string` or `pattern` has been reached and handles these cases appropriately.

3. **Pattern Matching Logic**:
   - It retrieves the current character from the `pattern`.
   - If the current pattern character is a space, it handles it as a wildcard:
     - If the next character in the pattern is also a space, it skips the current space (double spaces have the same effect as one space).
     - If the next character is not a space, it recursively checks if any substring from the current position in the `string` matches the rest of the `pattern`.
   - If the current pattern character is not a space, it checks if it matches the current character in the `string`. If not, it returns `false`.

4. **Character Comparison**:
   - If the current characters in both the `string` and `pattern` match, it moves to the next character in both.

5. **Return Value**:
   - The method returns `true` if the entire `pattern` matches the `string`, otherwise it returns `false`.

This method effectively uses recursion and wildcard handling to match patterns with strings, accommodating spaces as wildcards that can match any sequence of characters.
codeFunctions: private static boolean match (final CharSequence string,final CharSequence pattern,int sNdx,int pNdx) { int pLen = pattern.length ();if (pLen == 1) { if (pattern.charAt (0) == ' ') { // speed-up return true;} } int sLen = string.length ();boolean nextIsNotWildcard = false;while (true) { // check if end of string and/or pattern occurred if ((sNdx >= sLen)) { // end of string still may have pending '*' in pattern while ((pNdx < pLen) && (pattern.charAt (pNdx) == ' ')) { pNdx ++;} return pNdx >= pLen;} if (pNdx >= pLen) { // end of pattern, but not end of the string return false;} char p = pattern.charAt (pNdx);// pattern char // perform logic if (!nextIsNotWildcard) { if (p == ' ') { pNdx ++;nextIsNotWildcard = true;continue;} if (p == ' ') { sNdx ++;pNdx ++;continue;} if (p == ' ') { char pNext = 0;// next pattern char if (pNdx + 1 < pLen) { pNext = pattern.charAt (pNdx + 1);} if (pNext == ' ') { // double '*' have the same effect as one '*' pNdx ++;continue;} int i;pNdx ++;// find recursively if there is any substring from the end of the // line that matches the rest of the pattern !!! for (i = string.length ();i >= sNdx;i --) { if (match (string,pattern,i,pNdx)) { return true;} } return false;} } else { nextIsNotWildcard = false;} // check if pattern char and string char are equals if (p != string.charAt (sNdx)) { return false;} // everything matches for now, continue sNdx ++;pNdx ++;} }

originalComment: Resolves loading rules.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `resolveLoading` method determines whether to load a class using the parent class loader or the current class loader based on a `parentFirstStrategy` and specific rules (`loaderOnlyRules` and `parentOnlyRules`). It initializes two boolean flags, `withParent` and `withLoader`, to `true`. Depending on the `parentFirstStrategy`, it checks if the `className` matches any rules. If it matches `loaderOnlyRules`, it sets `withParent` to `false`. If it matches `parentOnlyRules`, it sets `withLoader` to `false`. The method returns a new `Loading` object with the resolved flags.
codeFunctions: protected Loading resolveLoading (final boolean parentFirstStrategy,final String className) { boolean withParent = true;boolean withLoader = true;if (parentFirstStrategy) { if (isMatchingRules (className,loaderOnlyRules)) { withParent = false;} else if (isMatchingRules (className,parentOnlyRules)) { withLoader = false;} } else { if (isMatchingRules (className,parentOnlyRules)) { withLoader = false;} else if (isMatchingRules (className,loaderOnlyRules)) { withParent = false;} } return new Loading (withParent,withLoader);}

originalComment: Loads class using parent - first or parent - last strategy.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `loadClass` method is an overridden and synchronized method responsible for loading a class by its name. It first checks if the class has already been loaded using `findLoadedClass`. If the class is found, it resolves the class if required and returns it. If the class is not loaded, it determines the loading strategy based on the `parentFirst` flag. If `parentFirst` is true, it attempts to load the class using the parent class loader first, and if that fails, it tries to load it using the current class loader. If `parentFirst` is false, it attempts to load the class using the current class loader first, and if that fails, it tries the parent class loader. If the class is still not found, it throws a `ClassNotFoundException`. After successfully loading the class, it resolves the class if required and returns it.
codeFunctions: @ Override protected synchronized Class <?> loadClass (final String className,final boolean resolve) throws ClassNotFoundException { // check first if the class has already been loaded Class <?> c = findLoadedClass (className);if (c != null) { if (resolve) { resolveClass (c);} return c;} // class not loaded yet Loading loading = resolveLoading (parentFirst,className);if (parentFirst) { // PARENT FIRST if (loading.withParent) { try { c = parentClassLoader.loadClass (className);} catch (ClassNotFoundException ignore) { } } if (c == null) { if (loading.withLoader) { c = this.findClass (className);} else { throw new ClassNotFoundException ("Class not found: " + className);} } } else { // THIS FIRST if (loading.withLoader) { try { c = this.findClass (className);} catch (ClassNotFoundException ignore) { } } if (c == null) { if (loading.withParent) { c = parentClassLoader.loadClass (className);} else { throw new ClassNotFoundException ("Class not found: " + className);} } } if (resolve) { resolveClass (c);} return c;}

originalComment: Returns a resource using parent - first or parent - last strategy.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `getResource` method is overridden to retrieve a resource URL based on the specified `resourceName`. It determines the search order (parent first or this class loader first) using the `resolveResourceLoading` method. If the search order is parent first, it attempts to load the resource from the parent class loader. If the resource is not found, it then tries to load it from the current class loader. If the search order is this class loader first, it attempts to load the resource from the current class loader. If the resource is not found, it then tries to load it from the parent class loader. The method returns the URL of the resource if found, or `null` if not found.
codeFunctions: @ Override public URL getResource (final String resourceName) { URL url = null;Loading loading = resolveResourceLoading (parentFirst,resourceName);if (parentFirst) { // PARENT FIRST if (loading.withParent) { url = parentClassLoader.getResource (resourceName);} if (url == null) { if (loading.withLoader) { url = this.findResource (resourceName);} } } else { // THIS FIRST if (loading.withLoader) { url = this.findResource (resourceName);} if (url == null) { if (loading.withParent) { url = parentClassLoader.getResource (resourceName);} } } return url;}

originalComment: Visits a type.
codeComment:
The method `visit` performs the following operations:
1. Retrieves a `ClassDescriptor` for a given `type` using `ClassIntrospector`.
2. If `classMetadataName` is not null, it processes a 'meta' field named `classMetadataName` by calling `onProperty` with `null` and `false` as arguments.
3. Obtains all property descriptors of the class using `getAllPropertyDescriptors`.
4. Iterates through each `PropertyDescriptor`:
   - Retrieves the `Getter` for the property, considering whether it is declared.
   - If a `Getter` exists, it retrieves the property name and checks if the property is transient by examining the field descriptor's modifiers.
   - Calls `onProperty` with the property name, the `PropertyDescriptor`, and a boolean indicating if the property is transient.
codeFunctions: public void visit () { ClassDescriptor classDescriptor = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (type);if (classMetadataName != null) { // process first 'meta' fields 'class' onProperty (classMetadataName,null,false);} PropertyDescriptor [ ] propertyDescriptors = classDescriptor.getAllPropertyDescriptors ();for (PropertyDescriptor propertyDescriptor:propertyDescriptors) { Getter getter = propertyDescriptor.getGetter (declared);if (getter != null) { String propertyName = propertyDescriptor.getName ();boolean isTransient = false;// check for transient flag FieldDescriptor fieldDescriptor = propertyDescriptor.getFieldDescriptor ();if (fieldDescriptor != null) { isTransient = Modifier.isTransient (fieldDescriptor.getField ().getModifiers ());} onProperty (propertyName,propertyDescriptor,isTransient);} } }

originalComment: Returns urls for the classloader
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `of` takes a `ClassLoader` and a `Class` as parameters and returns an array of `URL` objects. If the provided `Class` is `null`, it defaults to `ClassPathURLs.class`. If the `ClassLoader` is `null`, it defaults to the class loader of the provided class (or `ClassPathURLs.class` if the class is `null`). The method iterates through the class loader hierarchy, collecting URLs from `URLClassLoader` instances and using a helper method `classModuleUrl` to get URLs for other types of class loaders. The collected URLs are stored in a `LinkedHashSet` to ensure uniqueness and order, and are then converted to an array of `URL` objects before being returned.
codeFunctions: public static URL [ ] of (ClassLoader classLoader,Class clazz) { if (clazz == null) { clazz = ClassPathURLs.class;} if (classLoader == null) { classLoader = clazz.getClassLoader ();} final Set < URL > urls = new LinkedHashSet <> ();while (classLoader != null) { if (classLoader instanceof URLClassLoader) { final URLClassLoader urlClassLoader = (URLClassLoader) classLoader;return urlClassLoader.getURLs ();} final URL url = classModuleUrl (classLoader,clazz);if (url != null) { urls.add (url);} classLoader = classLoader.getParent ();} return urls.toArray (new URL [ 0 ]);}

codeComment:
### Summary:

originalComment: Creates a SSL socket.Enables default secure enabled protocols if specified.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `createSSLSocket` method creates and configures an `SSLSocket` for a given host and port with specified connection timeout settings. It uses a `SocketFactory` to create a socket, which is then wrapped in an `SSLSocket`. The method handles cases where a connection timeout is specified, creating a plain socket first and then wrapping it with SSL. It also configures the SSL socket to use specific enabled protocols and sets up an endpoint identification algorithm if HTTPS host verification is required. The method returns the configured `SSLSocket`.
codeFunctions: protected SSLSocket createSSLSocket (final String host,final int port,final int connectionTimeout,final boolean trustAll,final boolean verifyHttpsHost) throws IOException { final SocketFactory socketFactory = getSocketFactory (proxy,true,trustAll,connectionTimeout);final Socket socket;if (connectionTimeout < 0) { socket = socketFactory.createSocket (host,port);} else { // creates unconnected socket // unfortunately, this does not work always //			sslSocket = (SSLSocket) socketFactory.createSocket(); //			sslSocket.connect(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), connectionTimeout); // // Note: SSLSocketFactory has several create() methods. // Those that take arguments all connect immediately // and have no options for specifying a connection timeout. // // So, we have to create a socket and connect it (with a // connection timeout), then have the SSLSocketFactory wrap // the already-connected socket. // socket = Sockets.connect (host,port,connectionTimeout);//sock.setSoTimeout(readTimeout); //socket.connect(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), connectionTimeout); // continue to wrap this plain socket with ssl socket... } // wrap plain socket in an SSL socket SSLSocket sslSocket;if (socket instanceof SSLSocket) { sslSocket = (SSLSocket) socket;} else { if (socketFactory instanceof SSLSocketFactory) { sslSocket = (SSLSocket) ((SSLSocketFactory) socketFactory).createSocket (socket,host,port,true);} else { sslSocket = (SSLSocket) (getDefaultSSLSocketFactory (trustAll)).createSocket (socket,host,port,true);} } // sslSocket is now ready if (secureEnabledProtocols != null) { final String [ ] values = StringUtil.splitc (secureEnabledProtocols,' ');StringUtil.trimAll (values);sslSocket.setEnabledProtocols (values);} // set SSL parameters to allow host name verifier if (verifyHttpsHost) { final SSLParameters sslParams = new SSLParameters ();sslParams.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm ("HTTPS");sslSocket.setSSLParameters (sslParams);} return sslSocket;}

originalComment: Returns default SSL socket factory allowing setting trust managers.
codeComment: This method, `getDefaultSSLSocketFactory`, returns an `SSLSocketFactory` based on the `trustAllCertificates` flag. If `trustAllCertificates` is true, it creates an `SSLContext` with a trust manager that trusts all certificates, initializes it with a secure random number generator, and returns the socket factory from this context. If an exception occurs during this process, it throws an `IOException`. If `trustAllCertificates` is false, it returns the default `SSLSocketFactory`.
codeFunctions: protected SSLSocketFactory getDefaultSSLSocketFactory (final boolean trustAllCertificates) throws IOException { if (trustAllCertificates) { try { SSLContext sc = SSLContext.getInstance (sslProtocol);sc.init (null,TrustManagers.TRUST_ALL_CERTS,new java.security.SecureRandom ());return sc.getSocketFactory ();} catch (NoSuchAlgorithmException | KeyManagementException e) { throw new IOException (e);} } else { return (SSLSocketFactory) SSLSocketFactory.getDefault ();} }

originalComment: Returns socket factory based on proxy type and SSL requirements.
codeComment: This method, `getSocketFactory`, determines and returns an appropriate `SocketFactory` based on the provided `ProxyInfo`, SSL requirement, certificate trust policy, and connection timeout. It handles different proxy types (NONE, HTTP, SOCKS4, SOCKS5) and whether SSL is required. If SSL is needed and no proxy is used, it returns a default SSL socket factory, optionally trusting all certificates. For HTTP, SOCKS4, and SOCKS5 proxies, it returns a corresponding proxy socket factory with the specified connection timeout. If an unsupported proxy type is provided, it returns `null`.
codeFunctions: protected SocketFactory getSocketFactory (final ProxyInfo proxy,final boolean ssl,final boolean trustAllCertificates,final int connectionTimeout) throws IOException { switch (proxy.getProxyType ()) { case NONE:if (ssl) { return getDefaultSSLSocketFactory (trustAllCertificates);} else { return SocketFactory.getDefault ();} case HTTP:return new HTTPProxySocketFactory (proxy,connectionTimeout);case SOCKS4:return new Socks4ProxySocketFactory (proxy,connectionTimeout);case SOCKS5:return new Socks5ProxySocketFactory (proxy,connectionTimeout);default:return null;} }

If `count` is 0, it returns an empty string. Otherwise, it initializes a character array `result` of size `count`, fills it with random characters from the `chars` array using `rnd.nextInt(chars.length)`, and returns the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public String random (int count,final char [ ] chars) { if (count == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} final char [ ] result = new char [ count ];while (count -- > 0) { result [ count ] = chars [ rnd.nextInt (chars.length) ];} return new String (result);}

### Summary:
The method `random` generates a string of random characters. It takes three parameters: `count` (the number of characters in the resulting string), `start` (the starting character for the range of possible characters), and `end` (the ending character for the range of possible characters). If `count` is 0, it returns an empty string. Otherwise, it creates an array of characters of size `count`, fills it with random characters within the specified range, and returns the array as a string.
codeFunctions: public String random (int count,final char start,final char end) { if (count == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} final char [ ] result = new char [ count ];final int len = end - start + 1;while (count -- > 0) { result [ count ] = (char) (rnd.nextInt (len) + start);} return new String (result);}

originalComment: Creates random string whose length is the number of characters specified.Characters are chosen from the multiple sets defined by range pairs.All ranges must be in acceding order.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `randomRanges` method generates a string of random characters based on specified ranges. It takes an integer `count` indicating the number of characters to generate and a variable number of `char` arguments representing character ranges. The method first calculates the total length of all ranges and stores the cumulative lengths in an array. It then generates random characters within these ranges and constructs a string of the specified length using these characters. If `count` is zero, it returns an empty string.
codeFunctions: public String randomRanges (int count,final char ... ranges) { if (count == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} int i = 0;int len = 0;final int [ ] lens = new int [ ranges.length ];while (i < ranges.length) { int gap = ranges [ i + 1 ] - ranges [ i ] + 1;len += gap;lens [ i ] = len;i += 2;} final char [ ] result = new char [ count ];while (count -- > 0) { char c = 0;int r = rnd.nextInt (len);for (i = 0;i < ranges.length;i += 2) { if (r < lens [ i ]) { r += ranges [ i ];if (i != 0) { r -= lens [ i - 2 ];} c = (char) r;break;} } result [ count ] = c;} return new String (result);}

originalComment: Returns IP address as integer.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `getIpAsInt` takes a string representing an IP address, splits it into tokens using a space as a delimiter, and then converts these tokens into an integer representation of the IP address. It does this by iterating over each token, shifting the current integer value left by 8 bits, and adding the integer value of the token. The final integer value is returned, representing the IP address in a packed integer format. However, there seems to be a mistake in the code as it uses a space (' ') as a delimiter for splitting the IP address, which is incorrect; typically, a dot ('.') is used.
codeFunctions: public static int getIpAsInt (final String ipAddress) { int ipIntValue = 0;String [ ] tokens = StringUtil.splitc (ipAddress,' ');for (String token:tokens) { if (ipIntValue > 0) { ipIntValue <<= 8;} ipIntValue += Integer.parseInt (token);} return ipIntValue;}

originalComment: Checks given string against IP address v4 format.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `validateAgaintIPAdressV4Format` checks if a given string is in a valid IPv4 address format. It returns `false` if the input is `null` or if the string does not conform to the IPv4 address format rules. The method counts the number of segments separated by spaces (not dots, as might be expected for IPv4) and ensures each segment is a number between 0 and 255. It returns `true` only if there are exactly four such segments.
codeFunctions: public static boolean validateAgaintIPAdressV4Format (final String input) { if (input == null) { return false;} int hitDots = 0;char [ ] data = input.toCharArray ();for (int i = 0;i < data.length;i ++) { char c = data [ i ];int b = 0;do { if (c < ' ' || c > ' ') { return false;} b = (b * 10 + c) - 48;if (++ i >= data.length) { break;} c = data [ i ];} while (c != ' ');if (b > 255) { return false;} hitDots ++;} return hitDots == 4;}

originalComment: Creates a socket with a timeout.

originalComment: Detects if provided class name is a primitive type.Returns > = 0 number if so.
codeComment: The method `getPrimitiveClassNameIndex` takes a `String` parameter `className` and returns an `int`. It first checks if the `className` contains a space by finding the index of a space character. If a space is found (i.e., `dotIndex` is not `-1`), it returns `-1`. Otherwise, it performs a binary search on the `PRIMITIVE_TYPE_NAMES` array for the `className` and returns the index of the `className` if found, or a negative value if not found.

originalComment: Loads class by name.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `loadClass` method attempts to load a class by its name using different class loaders. It first checks if the class name corresponds to a primitive type. If not, it tries to load the class using the provided class loader, the current thread's class loader, and the caller's class loader. If all these attempts fail and the class name represents an array, it tries to load the class using an alternative array loader. If the class is still not found, it throws a `ClassNotFoundException`.
codeFunctions: @ Override public Class loadClass (final String className,final ClassLoader classLoader) throws ClassNotFoundException { String arrayClassName = prepareArrayClassnameForLoading (className);if ((className.indexOf (' ') == - 1) && (arrayClassName == null)) { // maybe a primitive int primitiveNdx = getPrimitiveClassNameIndex (className);if (primitiveNdx >= 0) { return PRIMITIVE_TYPES [ primitiveNdx ];} } // try #1 - using provided class loader if (classLoader != null) { Class klass = loadClass (className,arrayClassName,classLoader);if (klass != null) { return klass;} } // try #2 - using thread class loader ClassLoader currentThreadClassLoader = Thread.currentThread ().getContextClassLoader ();if ((currentThreadClassLoader != null) && (currentThreadClassLoader != classLoader)) { Class klass = loadClass (className,arrayClassName,currentThreadClassLoader);if (klass != null) { return klass;} } // try #3 - using caller classloader, similar as Class.forName() //Class callerClass = ReflectUtil.getCallerClass(2); Class callerClass = ClassUtil.getCallerClass ();ClassLoader callerClassLoader = callerClass.getClassLoader ();if ((callerClassLoader != classLoader) && (callerClassLoader != currentThreadClassLoader)) { Class klass = loadClass (className,arrayClassName,callerClassLoader);if (klass != null) { return klass;} } // try #4 - everything failed, try alternative array loader if (arrayClassName != null) { try { return loadArrayClassByComponentType (className,classLoader);} catch (ClassNotFoundException ignore) { } } throw new ClassNotFoundException ("Class not found: " + className);}

originalComment: Loads array class using component type.
codeComment: This method, `loadArrayClassByComponentType`, takes a class name and a class loader as parameters. It identifies the component type of the array from the class name and loads it using the provided class loader. The method then determines the number of dimensions of the array based on the number of spaces in the class name. It creates an array of the appropriate dimension with zero size in each dimension and returns the class of this array.
codeFunctions: protected Class loadArrayClassByComponentType (final String className,final ClassLoader classLoader) throws ClassNotFoundException { int ndx = className.indexOf (' ');int multi = StringUtil.count (className,' ');String componentTypeName = className.substring (0,ndx);Class componentType = loadClass (componentTypeName,classLoader);if (multi == 1) { return Array.newInstance (componentType,0).getClass ();} int [ ] multiSizes;if (multi == 2) { multiSizes = new int [ ] { 0,0 };} else if (multi == 3) { multiSizes = new int [ ] { 0,0,0 };} else { multiSizes = (int [ ]) Array.newInstance (int.class,multi);} return Array.newInstance (componentType,multiSizes).getClass ();}

originalComment: Creates binary search wrapper over an array.
codeComment: The method `forArray` is a generic static method that takes an array of elements of type `T`, where `T` extends `Comparable`. It returns a new instance of `BinarySearch<T>`. This instance overrides two methods: `compare` and `getLastIndex`. The `compare` method compares the element at a given index in the array with a specified element using the `compareTo` method of `T`. The `getLastIndex` method returns the last valid index of the array, which is `array.length - 1`.
codeFunctions: public static < T extends Comparable > BinarySearch < T > forArray (final T [ ] array) { return new BinarySearch < T > () { @ Override @ SuppressWarnings ({ "unchecked" }) protected int compare (final int index,final T element) { return array [ index ].compareTo (element);} @ Override protected int getLastIndex () { return array.length - 1;} };}

### Summary:
The method `forArray` is a generic static method that takes an array of type `T` and a `Comparator<T>` as parameters. It returns a new instance of `BinarySearch<T>`. This instance overrides two methods: `compare` and `getLastIndex`. The `compare` method uses the provided comparator to compare an element at a specified index in the array with a given element. The `getLastIndex` method returns the last valid index of the array, which is `array.length - 1`.
codeFunctions: public static < T > BinarySearch < T > forArray (final T [ ] array,final Comparator < T > comparator) { return new BinarySearch < T > () { @ Override @ SuppressWarnings ({ "unchecked" }) protected int compare (final int index,final T element) { return comparator.compare (array [ index ],element);} @ Override protected int getLastIndex () { return array.length - 1;} };}

originalComment: Resolves column db sql type and populates it in column descriptor if missing.
codeComment: This method, `resolveColumnDbSqlType`, determines the SQL type of a database column if it is not already known. It takes a `Connection` object and a `DbEntityColumnDescriptor` object as parameters. If the SQL type of the column is already set to a known value, the method returns immediately. Otherwise, it retrieves metadata about the column from the database using the `DatabaseMetaData` object obtained from the connection. If the column metadata is successfully retrieved, the SQL type is extracted from the `ResultSet` and set in the `DbEntityColumnDescriptor`. If the metadata cannot be retrieved or the column is not found, the SQL type is set to `DB_SQLTYPE_NOT_AVAILABLE`, and a warning is logged. The method ensures that the `ResultSet` is closed in the `finally` block to prevent resource leaks.
codeFunctions: protected void resolveColumnDbSqlType (final Connection connection,final DbEntityColumnDescriptor dec) { if (dec.dbSqlType != SqlType.DB_SQLTYPE_UNKNOWN) { return;} ResultSet rs = null;DbEntityDescriptor ded = dec.getDbEntityDescriptor ();try { DatabaseMetaData dmd = connection.getMetaData ();rs = dmd.getColumns (null,ded.getSchemaName (),ded.getTableName (),dec.getColumnName ());if (rs.next ()) { dec.dbSqlType = rs.getInt ("DATA_TYPE");} else { dec.dbSqlType = SqlType.DB_SQLTYPE_NOT_AVAILABLE;if (log.isWarnEnabled ()) { log.warn ("Column SQL type not available: " + ded.toString () + ' ' + dec.getColumnName ());} } } catch (SQLException sex) { dec.dbSqlType = SqlType.DB_SQLTYPE_NOT_AVAILABLE;if (log.isWarnEnabled ()) { log.warn ("Column SQL type not resolved: " + ded.toString () + ' ' + dec.getColumnName (),sex);} } finally { DbUtil.close (rs);} }

originalComment: Pre - process SQL before using it.If string starts with a non - ascii char or it has no spaces it will be loaded from the query map.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `preprocessSql` method processes a given SQL string by performing several checks and transformations:
1. It first checks if the SQL string starts with a space. If so, it returns the string as is.
2. If the string does not start with a space, it checks if the first character is not an alphabetic character. If true, it removes the first character from the string.
3. If the string starts with an alphabetic character and contains a space, it returns the string as is.
4. It then attempts to retrieve a pre-stored SQL query from a map using `dbOom.queryMap().getQuery(sqlString)`. If a query is found, it trims the retrieved string and assigns it back to `sqlString`.
5. Finally, it returns the processed `sqlString`.
codeFunctions: protected String preprocessSql (String sqlString) { // detects callable statement if (sqlString.charAt (0) == ' ') { return sqlString;} // quickly detect if SQL string is a key if (!CharUtil.isAlpha (sqlString.charAt (0))) { sqlString = sqlString.substring (1);} else if (sqlString.indexOf (' ') != - 1) { return sqlString;} final String sqlFromMap = dbOom.queryMap ().getQuery (sqlString);if (sqlFromMap != null) { sqlString = sqlFromMap.trim ();} return sqlString;}

originalComment: Populates entity with generated column values from executed query.
codeComment: The method `populateGeneratedKeys` populates generated key values into the provided entity object. It first retrieves the names of the generated columns. If no generated columns are found, it returns immediately. It then looks up the entity's descriptor and prepares arrays for key types and property names corresponding to the generated columns. For each generated column, it finds the column descriptor, retrieves the property type and name, and stores them in the respective arrays. After preparing the key types, it fetches the generated key values. If the key values are not an array, it sets the first property of the entity with the key values. If the key values are an array, it iterates through the properties and sets each property with the corresponding key value from the array.
codeFunctions: public void populateGeneratedKeys (final Object entity) { final String [ ] generatedColumns = getGeneratedColumnNames ();if (generatedColumns == null) { return;} DbEntityDescriptor ded = dbOom.entityManager ().lookupType (entity.getClass ());// prepare key types Class [ ] keyTypes = new Class [ generatedColumns.length ];String [ ] properties = new String [ generatedColumns.length ];for (int i = 0;i < generatedColumns.length;i ++) { String column = generatedColumns [ i ];DbEntityColumnDescriptor decd = ded.findByColumnName (column);if (decd != null) { keyTypes [ i ] = decd.getPropertyType ();properties [ i ] = decd.getPropertyName ();} } final Object keyValues = findGeneratedColumns (keyTypes);if (!keyValues.getClass ().isArray ()) { BeanUtil.declared.setProperty (entity,properties [ 0 ],keyValues);} else { for (int i = 0;i < properties.length;i ++) { BeanUtil.declared.setProperty (entity,properties [ i ],((Object [ ]) keyValues) [ i ]);} } }

originalComment: Sets bean parameters from bean.Non - existing bean properties are ignored.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `setBean` method sets properties of a given bean object onto a query object. It iterates through each named parameter in the query, checks if the parameter name starts with the specified bean name followed by a space, and if so, extracts the property name. If the bean has a property with the extracted name, it retrieves the property value and sets it in the query using the `setObject` method. If the bean is null, it simply returns the current instance without making any changes. The method initializes the query before processing the parameters and returns the current instance after setting the properties.
codeFunctions: public Q setBean (final String beanName,final Object bean) { if (bean == null) { return _this ();} init ();final String beanNamePrefix = beanName + ' ';query.forEachNamedParameter (p -> { final String paramName = p.name;if (paramName.startsWith (beanNamePrefix)) { final String propertyName = paramName.substring (beanNamePrefix.length ());if (BeanUtil.declared.hasRootProperty (bean,propertyName)) { final Object value = BeanUtil.declared.getProperty (bean,propertyName);setObject (paramName,value);} } });return _this ();}

It updates the `nextChunk` reference of the `previous` chunk to point to the current chunk, and the `previousChunk` reference of the current chunk to point back to the `previous` chunk. originalComment: Encode an array of binary bytes into a Base32 string.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `encode` method converts a byte array into a Base32 encoded string. It processes the input bytes in chunks, combining and shifting bits to fit into the Base32 character set. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the resulting string. For each byte, it performs a series of bitwise operations to extract and combine 5-bit segments, appending the corresponding Base32 characters from a predefined `CHARS` array. The process handles cases where the input byte array length is not a multiple of 5 by appending the remaining bits as a final character.
codeFunctions: public static String encode (final byte [ ] bytes) { StringBuilder base32 = new StringBuilder ((bytes.length * 8 + 4) / 5);int currByte,digit,i = 0;while (i < bytes.length) { // STEP 0; insert new 5 bits, leave 3 bits currByte = bytes [ i ++ ] & 255;base32.append (CHARS [ currByte >> 3 ]);digit = (currByte & 7) << 2;if (i >= bytes.length) { base32.append (CHARS [ digit ]);break;} // STEP 3: insert 2 new bits, then 5 bits, leave 1 bit currByte = bytes [ i ++ ] & 255;base32.append (CHARS [ digit | (currByte >> 6) ]);base32.append (CHARS [ (currByte >> 1) & 31 ]);digit = (currByte & 1) << 4;if (i >= bytes.length) { base32.append (CHARS [ digit ]);break;} // STEP 1: insert 4 new bits, leave 4 bit currByte = bytes [ i ++ ] & 255;base32.append (CHARS [ digit | (currByte >> 4) ]);digit = (currByte & 15) << 1;if (i >= bytes.length) { base32.append (CHARS [ digit ]);break;} // STEP 4: insert 1 new bit, then 5 bits, leave 2 bits currByte = bytes [ i ++ ] & 255;base32.append (CHARS [ digit | (currByte >> 7) ]);base32.append (CHARS [ (currByte >> 2) & 31 ]);digit = (currByte & 3) << 3;if (i >= bytes.length) { base32.append (CHARS [ digit ]);break;} // STEP 2: insert 3 new bits, then 5 bits, leave 0 bit currByte = bytes [ i ++ ] & 255;base32.append (CHARS [ digit | (currByte >> 5) ]);base32.append (CHARS [ currByte & 31 ]);} return base32.toString ();}

### Summary:
The `convertValueToArray` method converts various types of input values into a byte array. It handles different types of objects such as `Blob`, `File`, `Collection`, `Iterable`, and `CharSequence`. For `Blob`, it reads the bytes from the blob if its length is within the integer range. For `File`, it reads the file content into bytes. For `Collection` and `Iterable`, it converts each element to a byte and stores them in an array. For `CharSequence`, it splits the string into parts based on number delimiters and converts them into a byte array. If the input does not match any of these types, it converts the value into a single-element byte array. The method throws a `TypeConversionException` if any errors occur during the conversion process.
codeFunctions: protected byte [ ] convertValueToArray (final Object value) { if (value instanceof Blob) { final Blob blob = (Blob) value;try { final long length = blob.length ();if (length > Integer.MAX_VALUE) { throw new TypeConversionException ("Blob is too big.");} return blob.getBytes (1,(int) length);} catch (SQLException sex) { throw new TypeConversionException (value,sex);} } if (value instanceof File) { try { return FileUtil.readBytes ((File) value);} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new TypeConversionException (value,ioex);} } if (value instanceof Collection) { final Collection collection = (Collection) value;final byte [ ] target = new byte [ collection.size () ];int i = 0;for (final Object element:collection) { target [ i ] = convertType (element);i ++;} return target;} if (value instanceof Iterable) { final Iterable iterable = (Iterable) value;final ArrayList < Byte > byteArrayList = new ArrayList <> ();for (final Object element:iterable) { final byte convertedValue = convertType (element);byteArrayList.add (Byte.valueOf (convertedValue));} final byte [ ] array = new byte [ byteArrayList.size () ];for (int i = 0;i < byteArrayList.size ();i ++) { final Byte b = byteArrayList.get (i);array [ i ] = b.byteValue ();} return array;} if (value instanceof CharSequence) { final String [ ] strings = StringUtil.splitc (value.toString (),ArrayConverter.NUMBER_DELIMITERS);return convertArrayToArray (strings);} // everything else: return convertToSingleElementArray (value);}

originalComment: Determine if request is eligible for GZipping.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `isGzipEligible` method determines whether a given HTTP request is eligible for GZIP compression based on several criteria:

1. **Request Parameter Check**: It first checks if a specific request parameter (`requestParameterName`) is provided and not empty. If the parameter is present, it attempts to convert its value to a boolean using `Converter.get().toBooleanValue`. If the conversion is successful and the value is `true`, the method returns `true`.

2. **URI Extraction and Normalization**: The method extracts the request URI and converts it to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison.

3. **URI Matching**:
   - If no specific matches (`matches`) are defined, the method checks if any file extensions (`extensions`) are specified. If no extensions are specified, it defaults to `true`.
   - If extensions are specified, it extracts the file extension from the URI and checks if it matches any of the specified extensions.
   - If specific matches are defined, it checks if the URI contains any of these matches. If `wildcards` are enabled, it uses wildcard matching; otherwise, it performs a simple substring search.

4. **Exclusion Check**: If the URI matches the inclusion criteria, the method checks if it should be excluded based on the `excludes` list. Similar to the matching process, it uses wildcard matching if enabled, otherwise, it checks for substring presence.

5. **Return Result**: The method returns `true` if the URI is eligible for GZIP compression after passing all checks, otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: protected boolean isGzipEligible (final HttpServletRequest request) { // request parameter name if (requestParameterName.length () != 0) { String forceGzipString = request.getParameter (requestParameterName);if (forceGzipString != null) { return Converter.get ().toBooleanValue (forceGzipString,false);} } // extract uri String uri = request.getRequestURI ();if (uri == null) { return false;} uri = uri.toLowerCase ();boolean result = false;// check uri if (matches == null) { // match == * if (extensions == null) { // extensions == * return true;} // extension String extension = FileNameUtil.getExtension (uri);if (extension.length () > 0) { extension = extension.toLowerCase ();if (StringUtil.equalsOne (extension,extensions) != - 1) { result = true;} } } else { if (wildcards) { result = Wildcard.matchPathOne (uri,matches) != - 1;} else { for (String match:matches) { if (uri.contains (match)) { result = true;break;} } } } if ((result) && (excludes != null)) { if (wildcards) { if (Wildcard.matchPathOne (uri,excludes) != - 1) { result = false;} } else { for (String exclude:excludes) { if (uri.contains (exclude)) { result = false;// excludes founded break;} } } } return result;}

originalComment: Performs validation of provided validation context and appends violations.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `validate` method takes a `ValidationContext`, a target object, and a target name as input. It iterates over each entry in the `ValidationContext` map, where each entry contains a property name and a list of `Check` objects. For each property, it retrieves the corresponding value from the target object. It then creates a `ValidationConstraintContext` for the property and iterates over the associated `Check` objects. Each `Check` is evaluated based on its profiles and severity. If a `Check` passes these conditions, its associated `ValidationConstraint` is used to validate the property value. If the validation fails, a `Violation` is added. Finally, the method returns a list of all collected `Violation` objects.
codeFunctions: public List < Violation > validate (final ValidationContext ctx,final Object target,final String targetName) { for (Map.Entry < String,List < Check > > entry:ctx.map.entrySet ()) { String name = entry.getKey ();Object value = BeanUtil.declaredSilent.getProperty (target,name);String valueName = targetName != null?(targetName + ' ' + name):name;// move up ValidationConstraintContext vcc = new ValidationConstraintContext (this,target,valueName);for (Check check:entry.getValue ()) { String [ ] checkProfiles = check.getProfiles ();if (!matchProfiles (checkProfiles)) { continue;} if (check.getSeverity () < severity) { continue;} ValidationConstraint constraint = check.getConstraint ();if (!constraint.isValid (vcc,value)) { addViolation (new Violation (valueName,target,value,check));} } } return getViolations ();}

originalComment: Determine if any of checks profiles is among enabled profiles.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `matchProfiles` method checks if the provided profiles match the enabled profiles based on several conditions:
1. If `checkProfiles` is `null` or contains only the `ALL_PROFILES` string, it returns `true`.
2. If `enabledProfiles` is `null` or empty:
   - If `validateAllProfilesByDefault` is `true`, it returns `true`.
   - If `checkProfiles` is `null` or empty, it returns `true` if the default profile is enabled.
   - It iterates through `checkProfiles` and returns `true` if any profile is empty (considered as the default profile) or matches the `DEFAULT_PROFILE`.
3. If `enabledProfiles` is not empty:
   - If `checkProfiles` is `null` or empty, it checks if the default profile is in `enabledProfiles`.
   - It iterates through `checkProfiles`:
     - Trims leading spaces and sets flags based on the presence of a space at the start.
     - Checks if the profile is in `enabledProfiles`:
       - Returns `false` if the profile is not found and was marked as required.
       - Sets `result` to `true` if the profile is found and not marked as required.
4. Returns `result` indicating whether all specified profiles are matched.
codeFunctions: protected boolean matchProfiles (final String [ ] checkProfiles) { // test for all profiles if ((checkProfiles != null) && (checkProfiles.length == 1) && checkProfiles [ 0 ].equals (ALL_PROFILES)) { return true;} if (enabledProfiles == null || enabledProfiles.isEmpty ()) { if (validateAllProfilesByDefault) { return true;// all profiles are considered as enabled } // only default profile is enabled if ((checkProfiles == null) || (checkProfiles.length == 0)) { return true;} for (String profile:checkProfiles) { if (StringUtil.isEmpty (profile)) { return true;// default profile } if (profile.equals (DEFAULT_PROFILE)) { return true;} } return false;} // there are enabled profiles if ((checkProfiles == null) || (checkProfiles.length == 0)) { return enabledProfiles.contains (DEFAULT_PROFILE);} boolean result = false;for (String profile:checkProfiles) { boolean b = true;boolean must = false;if (StringUtil.isEmpty (profile)) { profile = DEFAULT_PROFILE;} else if (profile.charAt (0) == ' ') { profile = profile.substring (1);b = false;} else if (profile.charAt (0) == ' ') { profile = profile.substring (1);must = true;} if (enabledProfiles.contains (profile)) { if (!b) { return false;} result = true;} else { if (must) { return false;} } } return result;}

### Summary:
The `toMilliseconds` method calculates the time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (January 1, 1970) from a Julian Date (JD) representation. It first computes the fractional and integer parts of the Julian Date relative to the Julian Date of the Unix epoch (`JD_1970`). Each part is converted to milliseconds by multiplying with `MILLIS_IN_DAY`. A small adjustment (1 microsecond) is added or subtracted based on the sign of the computed milliseconds to handle precision issues. Finally, the result is cast to a `long` and returned.
codeFunctions: public long toMilliseconds () { double then = (fraction - JD_1970.fraction) * MILLIS_IN_DAY;then += (integer - JD_1970.integer) * MILLIS_IN_DAY;then += then > 0?1.0e-6:- 1.0e-6;return (long) then;}

originalComment: Sets integer and fractional part with normalization.Normalization means that if double is out of range values will be correctly fixed.
codeComment: The method `set` takes two parameters, an integer `i` and a double `f`. It sets the `integer` field to the value of `i`. It then extracts the integer part of `f` by casting it to an `int` and assigns it to `fi`. The fractional part of `f` is obtained by subtracting `fi` from `f`. This fractional part is then added to the `integer` field, effectively transferring any whole number part of the fractional component to the integer part. If the resulting fractional part `f` is negative, it adjusts `f` by adding 1 and decrements the `integer` field by 1 to maintain the correct integer and fractional representation. Finally, it sets the `fraction` field to the adjusted value of `f`.
codeFunctions: private void set (final int i,double f) { integer = i;int fi = (int) f;f -= fi;integer += fi;if (f < 0) { f += 1;integer --;} this.fraction = f;}

codeFunctions: protected void emitComment (final int from,final int to) { if (config.enableConditionalComments) { // CC: downlevel-hidden starting if (match (CC_IF,from)) { int endBracketNdx = find (' ',from + 3,to);CharSequence expression = charSequence (from + 1,endBracketNdx);ndx = endBracketNdx + 1;char c = input [ ndx ];if (c != ' ') { errorInvalidToken ();} visitor.condComment (expression,true,true,false);state = DATA_STATE;return;} if (to > CC_ENDIF2.length && match (CC_ENDIF2,to - CC_ENDIF2.length)) { // CC: downlevel-hidden ending visitor.condComment (_ENDIF,false,true,true);state = DATA_STATE;return;} } CharSequence comment = charSequence (from,to);visitor.comment (comment);commentStart = - 1;}

originalComment: Parses a JavaTypeSignature and makes the given visitor visit it.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `parseType` method is designed to parse a Java type signature string starting from a specified offset. It uses a `SignatureVisitor` to visit different components of the type signature such as base types, array types, type variables, and class types. The method handles various cases based on the initial character of the type signature:

1. **BaseType or VoidDescriptor**: If the character is a base type or void, it visits the base type using `signatureVisitor.visitBaseType(currentChar)` and returns the current offset.
2. **ArrayTypeSignature**: If the character is `[`, it recursively calls `parseType` to parse the array type, starting from the next character, and visits the array type using `signatureVisitor.visitArrayType()`.
3. **TypeVariableSignature**: If the character is `T`, it identifies the type variable by finding the next `;` and visits the type variable using `signatureVisitor.visitTypeVariable(signature.substring(offset, endOffset))`.
4. **ClassTypeSignature**: If the character is `L`, it parses the class type signature, which may include main and inner class names, and optional type arguments. It visits each class name using `signatureVisitor.visitClassType(name)` or `signatureVisitor.visitInnerClassType(name)` as appropriate. If type arguments are present, it parses them and visits each type argument using `signatureVisitor.visitTypeArgument()`.

The method throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if the initial character does not match any of the expected cases. The parsing continues until the end of the class type signature is reached, at which point it calls `signatureVisitor.visitEnd()` and returns the final offset.
codeFunctions: private static int parseType (final String signature,final int startOffset,final SignatureVisitor signatureVisitor) { int offset = startOffset;// Current offset in the parsed signature. char currentChar = signature.charAt (offset ++);// The signature character at 'offset'. // Switch based on the first character of the JavaTypeSignature, which indicates its kind. switch (currentChar) { case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':case ' ':// Case of a BaseType or a VoidDescriptor. signatureVisitor.visitBaseType (currentChar);return offset;case ' ':// Case of an ArrayTypeSignature, a '[' followed by a JavaTypeSignature. return parseType (signature,offset,signatureVisitor.visitArrayType ());case ' ':// Case of TypeVariableSignature, an identifier between 'T' and ';'. int endOffset = signature.indexOf (' ',offset);signatureVisitor.visitTypeVariable (signature.substring (offset,endOffset));return endOffset + 1;case ' ':// Case of a ClassTypeSignature, which ends with ';'. // These signatures have a main class type followed by zero or more inner class types // (separated by '.'). Each can have type arguments, inside '<' and '>'. int start = offset;// The start offset of the currently parsed main or inner class name. boolean visited = false;// Whether the currently parsed class name has been visited. boolean inner = false;// Whether we are currently parsing an inner class type. // Parses the signature, one character at a time. while (true) { currentChar = signature.charAt (offset ++);if (currentChar == ' ' || currentChar == ' ') { // If a '.' or ';' is encountered, this means we have fully parsed the main class name // or an inner class name. This name may already have been visited it is was followed by // type arguments between '<' and '>'. If not, we need to visit it here. if (!visited) { String name = signature.substring (start,offset - 1);if (inner) { signatureVisitor.visitInnerClassType (name);} else { signatureVisitor.visitClassType (name);} } // If we reached the end of the ClassTypeSignature return, otherwise start the parsing // of a new class name, which is necessarily an inner class name. if (currentChar == ' ') { signatureVisitor.visitEnd ();break;} start = offset;visited = false;inner = true;} else if (currentChar == ' ') { // If a '<' is encountered, this means we have fully parsed the main class name or an // inner class name, and that we now need to parse TypeArguments. First, we need to // visit the parsed class name. String name = signature.substring (start,offset - 1);if (inner) { signatureVisitor.visitInnerClassType (name);} else { signatureVisitor.visitClassType (name);} visited = true;// Now, parse the TypeArgument(s), one at a time. while ((currentChar = signature.charAt (offset)) != ' ') { switch (currentChar) { case ' ':// Unbounded TypeArgument. ++ offset;signatureVisitor.visitTypeArgument ();break;case ' ':case ' ':// Extends or Super TypeArgument. Use offset + 1 to skip the '+' or '-'. offset = parseType (signature,offset + 1,signatureVisitor.visitTypeArgument (currentChar));break;default:// Instanceof TypeArgument. The '=' is implicit. offset = parseType (signature,offset,signatureVisitor.visitTypeArgument (' '));break;} } } } return offset;default:throw new IllegalArgumentException ();} }

originalComment: Returns the size of the Module ModulePackages and ModuleMainClass attributes generated by this ModuleWriter.Also add the names of these attributes in the constant pool.
codeComment: The `computeAttributesSize` method calculates the total size of the module attributes in bytes. It starts by adding a constant UTF-8 entry for `Constants.MODULE` to the symbol table and initializes the size with 22 bytes, which account for the attribute header, name, flags, version, and counts. The size is then incremented by the lengths of `requires`, `exports`, `opens`, `usesIndex`, and `provides` arrays. If there are packages (`packageCount > 0`), it adds another constant UTF-8 entry for `Constants.MODULE_PACKAGES` and increases the size by 8 bytes plus the length of the `packageIndex` array. If a main class is specified (`mainClassIndex > 0`), it adds a constant UTF-8 entry for `Constants.MODULE_MAIN_CLASS` and increases the size by 8 bytes. Finally, the method returns the computed size.
codeFunctions: int computeAttributesSize () { symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE);// 6 attribute header bytes, 6 bytes for name, flags and version, and 5 * 2 bytes for counts. int size = 22 + requires.length + exports.length + opens.length + usesIndex.length + provides.length;if (packageCount > 0) { symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE_PACKAGES);// 6 attribute header bytes, and 2 bytes for package_count. size += 8 + packageIndex.length;} if (mainClassIndex > 0) { symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE_MAIN_CLASS);// 6 attribute header bytes, and 2 bytes for main_class_index. size += 8;} return size;}

originalComment: Puts the Module ModulePackages and ModuleMainClass attributes generated by this ModuleWriter in the given ByteVector.
codeComment: The `putAttributes` method writes module-related attributes to a `ByteVector` output. It starts by calculating the total length of the module attribute, which includes fixed-size fields and variable-length arrays for requires, exports, opens, uses, and provides. The method then writes the module attribute name, its length, module name index, module flags, module version index, and counts for requires, exports, opens, uses, and provides. It appends the corresponding byte arrays for each of these sections. If there are packages, it writes the package attribute name, its length, package count, and package index byte array. If a main class index is specified, it writes the main class attribute name, its length, and the main class index.
codeFunctions: void putAttributes (final ByteVector output) { // 6 bytes for name, flags and version, and 5 * 2 bytes for counts. int moduleAttributeLength = 16 + requires.length + exports.length + opens.length + usesIndex.length + provides.length;output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE)).putInt (moduleAttributeLength).putShort (moduleNameIndex).putShort (moduleFlags).putShort (moduleVersionIndex).putShort (requiresCount).putByteArray (requires.data,0,requires.length).putShort (exportsCount).putByteArray (exports.data,0,exports.length).putShort (opensCount).putByteArray (opens.data,0,opens.length).putShort (usesCount).putByteArray (usesIndex.data,0,usesIndex.length).putShort (providesCount).putByteArray (provides.data,0,provides.length);if (packageCount > 0) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE_PACKAGES)).putInt (2 + packageIndex.length).putShort (packageCount).putByteArray (packageIndex.data,0,packageIndex.length);} if (mainClassIndex > 0) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.MODULE_MAIN_CLASS)).putInt (2).putShort (mainClassIndex);} }

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `start` method initializes the database connection and related components if the database is enabled. It performs the following steps:

1. Initializes the logger.
2. Checks if the database is enabled; if not, logs a message and exits.
3. Retrieves a `PetiteContainer` instance.
4. Creates or retrieves a `connectionProvider` and adds it to the `PetiteContainer`.
5. Initializes the `connectionProvider` and checks its configuration.
6. Creates a `jtxManager` for transaction management and configures it.
7. Sets up an `AnnotationTxAdviceManager` for transactional advice.
8. Configures a proxy with transaction aspects.
9. Initializes a `DbSessionProvider` for session management.
10. Loads and logs the number of queries from a `QueryMap`.
11. Creates and configures a `DbOom` instance with the connection provider, session provider, and query map.
12. Connects to the database and resets the `DbEntityManager`.
13. Adds the query configuration and `DbOom` configuration to the `PetiteContainer`.
14. If auto-configuration is enabled, it sets up an `AutomagicDbOomConfigurator` and registers it as a consumer.
15. Accepts the `dbEntityManager` for further processing.
16. Logs a success message indicating that the database is ready.
codeFunctions: @ Override @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public void start () { initLogger ();if (!databaseEnabled) { log.info ("DB not enabled.");return;} log.info ("DB start ----------");final PetiteContainer petiteContainer = joyPetiteSupplier.get ().getPetiteContainer ();// connection pool connectionProvider = createConnectionProviderIfNotSupplied ();petiteContainer.addBean (beanNamePrefix () + "pool",connectionProvider);if (connectionProvider instanceof CoreConnectionPool) { final CoreConnectionPool pool = (CoreConnectionPool) connectionProvider;if (pool.getDriver () == null) { databaseEnabled = false;log.warn ("DB configuration not set (" + beanNamePrefix () + "pool.*). DB will be disabled.");return;} } connectionProvider.init ();checkConnectionProvider ();// transactions manager jtxManager = createJtxTransactionManager (connectionProvider);jtxManager.setValidateExistingTransaction (true);final AnnotationTxAdviceManager annTxAdviceManager = new AnnotationTxAdviceManager (new LeanJtxWorker (jtxManager),jtxScopePattern);AnnotationTxAdviceSupport.manager = annTxAdviceManager;// create proxy joyProxettaSupplier.get ().getProxetta ().withAspect (createTxProxyAspects (annTxAdviceManager.getAnnotations ()));final DbSessionProvider sessionProvider = new DbJtxSessionProvider (jtxManager);// querymap final long startTime = System.currentTimeMillis ();final QueryMap queryMap = new DbPropsQueryMap ();log.debug ("Queries loaded in " + (System.currentTimeMillis () - startTime) + "ms.");log.debug ("Total queries: " + queryMap.size ());// dboom dbOom = DbOom.create ().withConnectionProvider (connectionProvider).withSessionProvider (sessionProvider).withQueryMap (queryMap).get ();dbOom.connect ();final DbEntityManager dbEntityManager = dbOom.entityManager ();dbEntityManager.reset ();petiteContainer.addBean (beanNamePrefix () + "query",dbOom.queryConfig ());petiteContainer.addBean (beanNamePrefix () + "oom",dbOom.config ());// automatic configuration if (autoConfiguration) { final AutomagicDbOomConfigurator automagicDbOomConfigurator = new AutomagicDbOomConfigurator (dbEntityManager,true);automagicDbOomConfigurator.registerAsConsumer (joyScannerSupplier.get ().getClassScanner ());} dbEntityManagerConsumers.accept (dbEntityManager);log.info ("DB OK!");}

originalComment: Stores signatures for all super public methods not already overridden by target class.All this methods will be accepted for proxyfication.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `visitEnd` method performs several tasks related to class and interface inspection:

1. **Class Annotations Preparation**: Converts `classAnnotations` to an array and assigns it to `annotations`, then clears `classAnnotations`.

2. **Superclass and Interface Collection**:
   - Initializes `superList` and `allInterfaces` to store superclass names and interface names, respectively.
   - Adds interfaces from `nextInterfaces` to `allInterfaces`.

3. **Superclass Inspection**:
   - Iterates through the superclass hierarchy starting from `nextSupername`.
   - For each superclass, it reads the class file using `ClassReader` and processes it with `SuperClassVisitor`.
   - Adds the superclass name to `superList` and the `ClassReader` to `superClassReaders`.
   - Collects interfaces implemented by each superclass and adds them to `allInterfaces`.

4. **Interface Inspection**:
   - Initializes `todoInterfaces` with `allInterfaces` and `newCollectedInterfaces` to track interfaces to inspect and newly found interfaces.
   - Iterates through `todoInterfaces`, reads each interface using `ClassReader`, and processes it with `SuperClassVisitor`.
   - Collects new interfaces implemented by each interface and adds them to `newCollectedInterfaces`.
   - Continues this process until no new interfaces are found.

5. **Final Collection**:
   - Adds all interfaces from `todoInterfaces` to `allInterfaces`.
   - Converts `superList` to an array and assigns it to `superClasses`.

This method ensures that all superclasses and interfaces, including those inherited and implemented, are properly collected and processed.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void visitEnd () { // prepare class annotations if (classAnnotations != null) { annotations = classAnnotations.toArray (new AnnotationInfo [ 0 ]);classAnnotations = null;} List < String > superList = new ArrayList <> ();Set < String > allInterfaces = new HashSet <> ();if (nextInterfaces != null) { allInterfaces.addAll (nextInterfaces);} // check all public super methods that are not overridden in superclass while (nextSupername != null) { InputStream inputStream = null;ClassReader cr;try { inputStream = ClassLoaderUtil.getClassAsStream (nextSupername,classLoader);cr = new ClassReader (inputStream);} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new ProxettaException ("Unable to inspect super class: " + nextSupername,ioex);} finally { StreamUtil.close (inputStream);} superList.add (nextSupername);superClassReaders.add (cr);// remember the super class reader cr.accept (new SuperClassVisitor (),0);if (cr.getInterfaces () != null) { Collections.addAll (allInterfaces,cr.getInterfaces ());} } superClasses = superList.toArray (new String [ 0 ]);// check all interface methods that are not overridden in super-interface Set < String > todoInterfaces = new HashSet <> (allInterfaces);Set < String > newCollectedInterfaces = new HashSet <> ();while (true) { for (String next:todoInterfaces) { InputStream inputStream = null;ClassReader cr;try { inputStream = ClassLoaderUtil.getClassAsStream (next,classLoader);cr = new ClassReader (inputStream);} catch (IOException ioex) { throw new ProxettaException ("Unable to inspect super interface: " + next,ioex);} finally { StreamUtil.close (inputStream);} superClassReaders.add (cr);// remember the super class reader cr.accept (new SuperClassVisitor (),0);if (cr.getInterfaces () != null) { for (String newInterface:cr.getInterfaces ()) { if (!allInterfaces.contains (newInterface) &&!todoInterfaces.contains (newInterface)) { // new interface found newCollectedInterfaces.add (newInterface);} } } } // perform collection allInterfaces.addAll (todoInterfaces);if (newCollectedInterfaces.isEmpty ()) { // no new interface found break;} todoInterfaces.clear ();todoInterfaces.addAll (newCollectedInterfaces);newCollectedInterfaces.clear ();} }

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `toCsvString` method constructs a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) formatted string from a variable number of input objects. It iterates through each element, converting it to a string and checking for special characters or spaces that require quoting. If any special characters, spaces at the start or end, or specific special characters are found, the field is enclosed in quotes. Fields are separated by a predefined field separator, and the method returns the complete CSV string.
codeFunctions: public static String toCsvString (final Object ... elements) { StringBuilder line = new StringBuilder ();int last = elements.length - 1;for (int i = 0;i < elements.length;i ++) { if (elements [ i ] == null) { if (i != last) { line.append (FIELD_SEPARATOR);} continue;} String field = elements [ i ].toString ();// check for special cases int ndx = field.indexOf (FIELD_SEPARATOR);if (ndx == - 1) { ndx = field.indexOf (FIELD_QUOTE);} if (ndx == - 1) { if (field.startsWith (StringPool.SPACE) || field.endsWith (StringPool.SPACE)) { ndx = 1;} } if (ndx == - 1) { ndx = StringUtil.indexOfChars (field,SPECIAL_CHARS);} // add field if (ndx != - 1) { line.append (FIELD_QUOTE);} field = StringUtil.replace (field,StringPool.QUOTE,DOUBLE_QUOTE);line.append (field);if (ndx != - 1) { line.append (FIELD_QUOTE);} // last if (i != last) { line.append (FIELD_SEPARATOR);} } return line.toString ();}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `toStringArray` method processes a given string `line` to split it into an array of strings based on a field separator, while handling quoted fields correctly. It iterates through each character of the input string, checking for the field separator and field quotes. When a field separator is encountered outside of a quoted field, it adds the current field to a list. If a field quote is found, it toggles the `inQuotedField` flag to manage the quoted state. After processing the entire string, it adds the last field to the list and returns the list as an array of strings.
codeFunctions: public static String [ ] toStringArray (final String line) { List < String > row = new ArrayList <> ();boolean inQuotedField = false;int fieldStart = 0;final int len = line.length ();for (int i = 0;i < len;i ++) { char c = line.charAt (i);if (c == FIELD_SEPARATOR) { if (!inQuotedField) { // ignore we are quoting addField (row,line,fieldStart,i,inQuotedField);fieldStart = i + 1;} } else if (c == FIELD_QUOTE) { if (inQuotedField) { if (i + 1 == len || line.charAt (i + 1) == FIELD_SEPARATOR) { // we are already quoting - peek to see if this is the end of the field addField (row,line,fieldStart,i,inQuotedField);fieldStart = i + 2;i ++;// and skip the comma inQuotedField = false;} } else if (fieldStart == i) { inQuotedField = true;// this is a beginning of a quote fieldStart ++;// move field start } } } // add last field - but only if string was not empty if (len > 0 && fieldStart <= len) { addField (row,line,fieldStart,len,inQuotedField);} return row.toArray (new String [ 0 ]);}

### Summary:
The `resolve` method determines the constructor to be used for dependency injection in a given class. It first retrieves all constructors of the class and checks for a default constructor (one with no parameters). If `useAnnotation` is true, it looks for a constructor annotated as an injection point. If multiple constructors are annotated, it throws a `PetiteException`. If no annotated constructor is found, it selects the default constructor or the only constructor if there is only one. If no suitable constructor is found and the bean is not already instantiated, it returns an empty `CtorInjectionPoint`.
