originalComment: Invocation handler implementation.Every method invocation on managed class interface is routed to this point.Here actual container services are implemented and method is invoked against wrapped instance.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `invoke` method is an overridden method that handles the invocation of a managed method on a proxy object. It first retrieves the `ManagedMethodSPI` instance corresponding to the method being invoked. If the method is not transactional, it directly invokes the method on the managed instance and handles any exceptions that occur. If the method is transactional, it checks if the method is immutable. If it is, it executes the method within an immutable transaction; otherwise, it executes it within a mutable transaction. The method logs the invocation and throws a detailed exception if a non-transactional method invocation fails.
codeFunctions: @ Override public Object invoke (Object proxy,Method method,Object [ ] args) throws Throwable { final ManagedMethodSPI managedMethod = managedClass.getManagedMethod (method);log.trace ("Invoke |%s|.",managedMethod);if (!managedMethod.isTransactional ()) { // execute managed method that is not included within transactional boundaries try { return managedMethod.invoke (managedInstance,args);} catch (Throwable t) { throw throwable (t,"Non transactional method |%s| invocation fails.",managedMethod);} } if (managedMethod.isImmutable ()) { return executeImmutableTransaction (managedMethod,args);} return executeMutableTransaction (managedMethod,args);}

originalComment: Helper method for mutable transaction execution.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `executeMutableTransaction` method manages a mutable transaction for a given `ManagedMethodSPI` instance. It starts by creating a transaction and storing its session on the current thread using a `transactionalResource`. The method then attempts to invoke the `managedMethod` with the provided arguments. If the method execution is successful, it commits the transaction. If the transaction was not used, it logs a debug message indicating that the method was unnecessarily declared as transactional. In case of any exceptions during the method invocation, it rolls back the transaction and rethrows the exception with a detailed message. Finally, it ensures that the transaction session is released from the current thread only if the outermost transaction is closed, handling potential nested transactions appropriately.
codeFunctions: private Object executeMutableTransaction (ManagedMethodSPI managedMethod,Object [ ] args) throws Throwable { // store transaction session on current thread via transactional resource utility // it may happen to have multiple nested transaction on current thread // since all are created by the same transactional resource, all are part of the same session // and there is no harm if storeSession is invoked multiple times // also performance penalty is comparable with the effort to prevent this multiple write Transaction transaction = transactionalResource.createTransaction ();transactionalResource.storeSession (transaction.getSession ());try { Object result = managedMethod.invoke (managedInstance,args);transaction.commit ();if (transaction.unused ()) { log.debug ("Method |%s| superfluously declared transactional.",managedMethod);} return result;} catch (Throwable throwable) { transaction.rollback ();throw throwable (throwable,"Mutable transactional method |%s| invocation fail.",managedMethod);} finally { if (transaction.close ()) { // it may happen to have multiple nested transaction on this thread // if this is the case, remove session from current thread only if outermost transaction is closed // of course if not nested transactions, remove at once transactionalResource.releaseSession ();} } }

originalComment: Helper method for immutable transaction execution.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `executeImmutableTransaction` method is designed to execute a method within an immutable (read-only) transactional context. It begins by creating a read-only transaction using `transactionalResource.createReadOnlyTransaction()`. The session associated with this transaction is then stored via `transactionalResource.storeSession(transaction.getSession())`. The method proceeds to invoke the target method (`managedMethod`) with the provided arguments (`args`). If the transaction is unused (i.e., no changes were made), a debug log is generated indicating that the method was unnecessarily declared as transactional. The result of the method invocation is returned. If an exception occurs during the method invocation, it is rethrown with a detailed error message. Finally, the method ensures that the transaction is properly closed, and if it was successfully closed, the session is released using `transactionalResource.releaseSession()`.
codeFunctions: private Object executeImmutableTransaction (ManagedMethodSPI managedMethod,Object [ ] args) throws Throwable { Transaction transaction = transactionalResource.createReadOnlyTransaction ();// see mutable transaction comment transactionalResource.storeSession (transaction.getSession ());try { Object result = managedMethod.invoke (managedInstance,args);if (transaction.unused ()) { log.debug ("Method |%s| superfluously declared transactional.",managedMethod);} return result;} catch (Throwable throwable) { throw throwable (throwable,"Immutable transactional method |%s| invocation fail.",managedMethod);} finally { if (transaction.close ()) { // see mutable transaction comment transactionalResource.releaseSession ();} } }

originalComment: Handle request for a resource.Locate resource method based on request path from request context execute method and serialize back to client returned resource.See class description for general behavior.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `handleRequest` method processes an HTTP request within a servlet context. It retrieves the request and response objects, then attempts to find and invoke the appropriate method based on the request path. If the method is not found, it throws a `NoSuchMethodException`. The method reads arguments from the request, invokes the method on a controller instance, and handles the result.

The method includes exception handling for various scenarios:
- **AuthorizationException**: Redirects to a login page if configured; otherwise, uses the servlet container's authentication mechanism.
- **NoSuchMethodException or IllegalArgumentException**: Sends a 404 Not Found error.
- **InvocationException**: Sends a 404 Not Found error if the cause is a `NoSuchResourceException`; otherwise, sends a 500 Internal Server Error.

After processing, the method sets the response status to 200 OK and serializes the resource to the response. The `argumentsReader` is cleaned up in the `finally` block to ensure resources are released.
codeFunctions: @ Override protected void handleRequest (RequestContext context) throws ServletException,IOException { // for exceptions generated before response commit uses HttpServletResponse.sendError // on send error, servlet container prepares error response using container internal HTML for response body // if <error-page> is configured into deployment descriptor servlet container uses that HTML for response body final HttpServletRequest httpRequest = context.getRequest ();final HttpServletResponse httpResponse = context.getResponse ();ArgumentsReader argumentsReader = null;Resource resource = null;try { ManagedMethodSPI method = resourceMethods.get (key (context.getRequestPath ()));if (method == null) { throw new NoSuchMethodException (httpRequest.getRequestURI ());} final Type [ ] formalParameters = method.getParameterTypes ();argumentsReader = argumentsReaderFactory.getArgumentsReader (httpRequest,formalParameters);Object [ ] arguments = argumentsReader.read (httpRequest,formalParameters);Object controller = container.getInstance (method.getDeclaringClass ());resource = method.invoke (controller,arguments);if (resource == null) { throw new BugError ("Null resource |%s|.",httpRequest.getRequestURI ());} } catch (AuthorizationException e) { // at this point, resource is private and need to redirect to a login page // if application provides one, tiny container is configured with, and use it // otherwise servlet container should have one // if no login page found send back servlet container error - that could be custom error page, if declared String loginPage = container.getLoginPage ();if (loginPage != null) { httpResponse.sendRedirect (loginPage);} else { // expected servlet container behavior: // if <login-config> section exist into web.xml do what is configured there // else send back internal page with message about SC_UNAUTHORIZED // authenticate can throw ServletException if fails, perhaps because is not configured // let servlet container handle this error, that could be custom error page is configured httpRequest.authenticate (httpResponse);} return;} catch (NoSuchMethodException | IllegalArgumentException e) { // do not use AppServlet#sendError since it is encoded JSON and for resources need HTML dumpError (context,e);httpResponse.sendError (HttpServletResponse.SC_NOT_FOUND,httpRequest.getRequestURI ());return;} catch (InvocationException e) { // do not use AppServlet#sendError since it is encoded JSON and for resources need HTML dumpError (context,e);if (e.getCause () instanceof NoSuchResourceException) { httpResponse.sendError (HttpServletResponse.SC_NOT_FOUND,httpRequest.getRequestURI ());} else { httpResponse.sendError (HttpServletResponse.SC_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,e.getCause ().getMessage ());} return;} finally { if (argumentsReader != null) { argumentsReader.clean ();} } // once serialization process started response becomes committed // and is not longer possible to use HttpServletResponse#sendError // let servlet container handle IO exceptions but since client already start rendering // there is no so much to do beside closing or reseting connection httpResponse.setStatus (HttpServletResponse.SC_OK);resource.serialize (httpResponse);}

originalComment: Closes all event streams still opened when event stream manager is destroyed.
codeComment: Summary: The `preDestroy` method ensures that all `EventStream` objects in the `eventStreams` list are properly closed. It first checks if the list is empty and returns immediately if so. To handle potential concurrent modifications, it converts the list to an array using `toArray(new EventStream[0])`. It then iterates over this array, logging a debug message for each `EventStream` and calling its `close` method to terminate the stream. This process effectively ends any ongoing request processing associated with these streams and removes them from the `eventStreams` list.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void preDestroy () { if (eventStreams.isEmpty ()) { return;} // EventStream#close signals stream loop that breaks // as a consequence, EventStreamServlet ends current request processing and call this#closeEventStream // this#closeEventStream removes event stream from this#eventStreams list resulting in concurrent change // to cope with this concurrent change uses a temporary array // toArray API is a little confusing for me regarding returned array // to be on safe side let toArray to determine array size // also I presume returned array is not altered by list updates for (EventStream eventStream:eventStreams.toArray (new EventStream [ 0 ])) { log.debug ("Force close stale event stream |%s|.",eventStream);eventStream.close ();} }

originalComment: Create views meta pool from given managed view configuration object.Configuration object is described on class description.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `config` method processes configuration settings for repositories, specifically focusing on view management. It iterates through each `<repository>` section in the provided `Config` object. For each repository, it performs the following steps:

1. **Load and Validate Implementation Class:**
   - Retrieves the class name from the `class` attribute of the repository section.
   - Attempts to load the class and checks if it is a subclass of `View`, instantiable, and not abstract or an interface.

2. **Extract Repository Path and Files Pattern:**
   - Retrieves the `path` and `files-pattern` attributes from the repository section.
   - Throws a `ConfigException` if either attribute is missing.

3. **Initialize I18N Repository:**
   - Uses the extracted path and files pattern to create an `I18nRepository` instance.
   - Initializes the `viewsMetaPool` with the pool instance from the first repository if it hasn't been set yet.

4. **Register View Meta Instances:**
   - Iterates through all files in the `I18nRepository`.
   - For each file, creates a `ViewMeta` instance using the file, the previously loaded view implementation class, and the properties from the repository section.
   - Registers the `ViewMeta` instance in the `viewsMetaPool`, logging a warning if an existing view is overridden and a debug message if a new view is registered.

This method ensures that all necessary configurations are correctly set up and that view implementations are properly validated and registered.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void config (Config config) throws ConfigException,IOException { for (Config repositorySection:config.findChildren ("repository")) { // view manager configuration section is named <views> // a <views> configuration section has one or many <repository> child sections // scan every repository files accordingly files pattern and add meta views to views meta pool // load repository view implementation class and perform insanity checks String className = repositorySection.getAttribute ("class",DEF_IMPLEMENTATION);Class <?> implementation = Classes.forOptionalName (className);if (implementation == null) { throw new ConfigException ("Unable to load view implementation |%s|.",className);} if (!Types.isKindOf (implementation,View.class)) { throw new ConfigException ("View implementation |%s| is not of proper type.",className);} if (!Classes.isInstantiable (implementation)) { throw new ConfigException ("View implementation |%s| is not instantiable. Ensure is not abstract or interface and have default constructor.",implementation);} @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") Class <?extends View > viewImplementation = (Class <?extends View >) implementation;// load repository path and files pattern and create I18N repository instance String repositoryPath = repositorySection.getAttribute ("path");if (repositoryPath == null) { throw new ConfigException ("Invalid views repository configuration. Missing <path> attribute.");} String filesPattern = repositorySection.getAttribute ("files-pattern");if (filesPattern == null) { throw new ConfigException ("Invalid views repository configuration. Missing <files-pattern> attribute.");} ConfigBuilder builder = new I18nRepository.ConfigBuilder (repositoryPath,filesPattern);I18nRepository repository = new I18nRepository (builder.build ());if (viewsMetaPool == null) { // uses first repository to initialize i18n pool // limitation for this solution is that all repositories should be the kind: locale sensitive or not viewsMetaPool = repository.getPoolInstance ();} Properties properties = repositorySection.getProperties ();// traverses all files from I18N repository instance and register view meta instance // builder is used by view meta to load the document template for (I18nFile template:repository) { ViewMeta meta = new ViewMeta (template.getFile (),viewImplementation,properties);if (viewsMetaPool.put (meta.getName (),meta,template.getLocale ())) { log.warn ("Override view |%s|",meta);} else { log.debug ("Register view |%s|",meta);} } } }

originalComment: Find the next clear bit in the bit set.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `nextClearBit` method finds the index of the next clear (0) bit in a bitset, starting from a given index. It first calculates the word index (`i`) and the sub-index (`subIndex`) within that word. It then inverts the bits of the word at index `i` and shifts right by `subIndex` to skip bits to the right of the starting index. If the resulting word is not zero, it calculates the position of the first clear bit using `Long.numberOfTrailingZeros` and returns the full index. If no clear bit is found in the current word, it continues to the next word until it either finds a clear bit or exhausts all words, in which case it returns -1.
codeFunctions: public int nextClearBit (int index) { int i = index >> 6;if (i >= wlen) return - 1;int subIndex = index & 0x3f;// index within the word long word = ~ bits.get (i) >> subIndex;// skip all the bits to the right of // index if (word != 0) { return (i << 6) + subIndex + Long.numberOfTrailingZeros (word);} while (++ i < wlen) { word = ~ bits.get (i);if (word != 0) { return (i << 6) + Long.numberOfTrailingZeros (word);} } return - 1;}

originalComment: Thread safe set operation that will set the bit if and only if the bit was not previously set.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `set` attempts to set a bit at a specified index in a bitset using an atomic operation. It calculates the word number and the bit position within that word. A bitmask is created to represent the bit to be set. The method then enters a loop where it retrieves the current word, checks if the bit is already set (indicating another thread may have set it), and if not, it sets the bit and attempts to update the word atomically. If the update is successful, it returns `true`; otherwise, it retries the process. If the bit was already set, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public boolean set (int index) { int wordNum = index >> 6;// div 64 int bit = index & 0x3f;// mod 64 long bitmask = 1L << bit;long word,oword;do { word = bits.get (wordNum);// if set another thread stole the lock if ((word & bitmask) != 0) { return false;} oword = word;word |= bitmask;} while (!bits.compareAndSet (wordNum,oword,word));return true;}

It first checks if the buffer is `null` and returns immediately if so. If unmapping is supported, it uses `AccessController.doPrivileged` to invoke the `cleaner` method on the buffer, which is then used to clean (unmap) the buffer. If an exception occurs during this process, it throws an `IOException` with a message indicating the failure to unmap the buffer.

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `deregisterWorker` method is responsible for removing a `ForkJoinWorkerThread` from the pool and cleaning up its associated resources. Here's a step-by-step summary of the method:

1. **Retrieve WorkQueue**: It first checks if the `ForkJoinWorkerThread` (`wt`) and its associated `WorkQueue` (`w`) are not null.

2. **Remove from Array**: It locks the run state, retrieves the `workQueues` array, and removes the `WorkQueue` from the array at the index specified by the worker's configuration.

3. **Decrement Counts**: It atomically decrements the active and total worker counts in the control (`ctl`) field.

4. **Cancel Tasks**: If the `WorkQueue` is not null, it sets the queue lock to -1, transfers steal counts, and cancels all remaining tasks in the queue.

5. **Replace Worker**: It enters a loop to potentially replace the worker:
   - If the pool is already terminating, it breaks out of the loop.
   - If there are still active workers, it tries to wake up a replacement worker.
   - If an exception was provided and the pool is configured to add workers, it attempts to add a new worker.
   - If no replacement is needed, it breaks out of the loop.

6. **Handle Exception**: If no exception was provided, it helps clean up stale exceptions. If an exception was provided, it rethrows the exception.

This method ensures that the worker is properly removed and that the pool's state is correctly updated, including handling any necessary replacements and cleanup.

### Summary:
The `signalWork` method is designed to activate idle workers in a work queue system. It checks the control state (`ctl`) to determine if there are too few active workers. If no idle workers are found and the control state indicates a need for more workers, it attempts to add a new worker. The task sets the sent date of the email, attempts to send it, and returns `true` if successful or `false` if an exception occurs, logging the error in both cases.

If `asynchronousSend` is false, the method attempts to send the email synchronously. It sets the sent date, tries to send the email, and logs an error if an exception occurs. codeFunctions: public static String encodeString (String value) { int estimatedSize = 0;final int len = value.length ();// estimate output string size to find out whether encoding is required and avoid reallocations in string builder for (int i = 0;i < len;++ i) { final char ch = value.charAt (i);if (ch <= ' ' || ch == ' ') { estimatedSize += 3;continue;} ++ estimatedSize;} if (value.length () == estimatedSize) { return value;// return value as is - it does not contain any special characters } final StringBuilder builder = new StringBuilder (estimatedSize);for (int i = 0;i < len;++ i) { final char ch = value.charAt (i);if (ch <= ' ') { builder.append ("%20");continue;} if (ch == ' ') { builder.append ("%2c");continue;} builder.append (ch);} return builder.toString ();}

codeFunctions: public static Optional < Charset > charset (File file) { if (!file.exists ()) { logger.error ("The file [ {} ] is not exist.",file.getAbsolutePath ());return Optional.absent ();} FileInputStream fileInputStream = null;BufferedInputStream bin = null;try { fileInputStream = new FileInputStream (file);bin = new BufferedInputStream (fileInputStream);int p = (bin.read () << 8) + bin.read ();Optional < Charset > charset;//其中的 0xefbb、0xfffe、0xfeff、0x5c75这些都是这个文件的前面两个字节的16进制数 switch (p) { case 0xefbb:charset = Optional.of (Charsets.UTF_8);break;case 0xfffe:charset = Optional.of (Charset.forName ("Unicode"));break;case 0xfeff:charset = Optional.of (Charsets.UTF_16BE);break;case 0x5c75:charset = Optional.of (Charsets.US_ASCII);break;default:charset = Optional.of (Charset.forName ("GBK"));} return charset;} catch (FileNotFoundException e) { logger.error ("The file [ {} ] is not exist.",file.getAbsolutePath (),e);} catch (IOException e) { logger.error ("Read file has error, {}.",file.getAbsolutePath (),e);} finally { IOUtils.closeQuietly (fileInputStream);IOUtils.closeQuietly (bin);} return Optional.absent ();}

It uses two regular expressions: `telcheck` for telephone numbers in the format of 3 or 4 digits, optionally followed by a hyphen, and then 7 to 9 digits; and `mobilecheck` for mobile numbers starting with specific prefixes (13x, 15x, 18x) followed by 8 more digits. The method returns `true` if the input string matches either of these patterns, ignoring case sensitivity, and `false` otherwise.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isPhone (String value) { String telcheck = "^\\d{3,4}-?\\d{7,9}$";String mobilecheck = "^(((13[0-9]{1})|(15[0-9]{1})|(18[0-9]{1}))+\\d{8})$";return match (telcheck,Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE,value) || match (mobilecheck,Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE,value);}

originalComment: Judge whether it is birthday
codeComment: The method `isBirthDay` checks if a given string `value` represents a valid date in the format `YYYY/MM/DD`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `YYYY.MM.DD`. It first uses a regular expression to ensure the string matches the expected date format. If the format is correct, it extracts the year, month, and day from the string. The method then validates the month and day values, ensuring they fall within the appropriate ranges. It specifically checks for invalid days in months with fewer than 31 days and handles leap year logic for February. If all checks pass, the method returns `true`, indicating a valid date; otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isBirthDay (String value) { String check = "(\\d{4})(/|-|\\.)(\\d{1,2})(/|-|\\.)(\\d{1,2})$";if (match (check,Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE,value)) { int year = Integer.parseInt (value.substring (0,4));int month = Integer.parseInt (value.substring (5,7));int day = Integer.parseInt (value.substring (8,10));if (month < 1 || month > 12) { return false;} if (day < 1 || day > 31) { return false;} if ((month == 4 || month == 6 || month == 9 || month == 11) && day == 31) { return false;} if (month == 2) { boolean isleap = (year % 4 == 0 && (year % 100 != 0 || year % 400 == 0));if (day > 29 || (day == 29 &&!isleap)) { return false;} } return true;} else { return false;} }

originalComment: Matches are linked

originalComment: Tell the time
codeComment:
### Summary:
The method `isDateTime` checks if a given string `value` matches a specific date-time pattern. The pattern allows for various date and time formats, including different separators (slash, hyphen, dot, or Chinese characters for year, month, and day) and optional time components (hour, minute, second) with optional Chinese characters. The method uses a regular expression to perform the match and returns a boolean indicating whether the string matches the pattern. The matching is case-insensitive.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isDateTime (String value) { String check = "^(\\d{4})(/|-|\\.|年)(\\d{1,2})(/|-|\\.|月)(\\d{1,2})(日)?(\\s+\\d{1,2}(:|时)\\d{1,2}(:|分)?(\\d{1,2}(秒)?)?)?$";// check =  " ^(\\d{4})(/|-|\\.)(\\d{1,2})(/|-|\\.)(\\d{1,2})$"; return match (check,Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE,value);}

originalComment: If targetLocation does not exist it will be created.
codeComment: The `copyDirectory` method is designed to recursively copy the contents of a source directory to a target directory. If the source is a directory, it checks if the target directory exists and creates it if it does not. It then iterates over each child in the source directory and recursively calls `copyDirectory` for each child. If the source is a file, it attempts to copy the file to the target location using a `write` method (which is assumed to be defined elsewhere in the code). If an `IOException` occurs during the file copy process, it throws an `UnexpectedException` with the original exception as its cause.
codeFunctions: public static void copyDirectory (File source,File target) { if (source.isDirectory ()) { if (!target.exists ()) { target.mkdir ();} for (String child:source.list ()) { copyDirectory (new File (source,child),new File (target,child));} } else { try { write (new FileInputStream (source),new FileOutputStream (target));} catch (IOException e) { throw new UnexpectedException (e);} } }

originalComment: Serialize to XML String

The method employs `TransformerFactory` and `Transformer` to perform the serialization process, transforming the `DOMSource` (which wraps the `Document`) into a `StreamResult` (which writes to the `StringWriter`). If a `TransformerException` occurs during this process, it is caught and rethrown as a `RuntimeException` with an appropriate error message. The method finally returns the XML content as a string.
codeFunctions: public static String serialize (Document document) { StringWriter writer = new StringWriter ();try { TransformerFactory factory = TransformerFactory.newInstance ();Transformer transformer = factory.newTransformer ();DOMSource domSource = new DOMSource (document);StreamResult streamResult = new StreamResult (writer);transformer.transform (domSource,streamResult);} catch (TransformerException e) { throw new RuntimeException ("Error when serializing XML document.",e);} return writer.toString ();}

originalComment: Check the xmldsig signature of the XML document.
codeComment: The method `validSignature` verifies the XML signature of a given `Document` using a provided `publicKey`. It retrieves the signature node from the document, sets up a key selector with the public key, and initializes an XML signature factory. A validation context is created, and the signature is unmarshalled and validated. If any exceptions occur during this process, a warning is logged, and the method returns `false`. If the validation is successful, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean validSignature (Document document,Key publicKey) { Node signatureNode = document.getElementsByTagNameNS (XMLSignature.XMLNS,"Signature").item (0);KeySelector keySelector = KeySelector.singletonKeySelector (publicKey);try { String providerName = System.getProperty ("jsr105Provider","org.jcp.xml.dsig.internal.dom.XMLDSigRI");XMLSignatureFactory fac = XMLSignatureFactory.getInstance ("DOM",(Provider) Class.forName (providerName).newInstance ());DOMValidateContext valContext = new DOMValidateContext (keySelector,signatureNode);XMLSignature signature = fac.unmarshalXMLSignature (valContext);return signature.validate (valContext);} catch (Exception e) { logger.warn ("Error validating an XML signature.",e);return false;} }

originalComment: Sign the XML document using xmldsig.
codeComment: The method `sign` takes an XML `Document` and RSA keys (`RSAPublicKey` and `RSAPrivateKey`) as input. It uses the `XMLSignatureFactory` to create a digital signature for the document. The process involves creating a `Reference` to the document content, specifying a digest method (SHA1), and applying an enveloped transform. A `SignedInfo` object is then created, which includes a canonicalization method (inclusive), a signature method (RSA_SHA1), and the previously created reference. The `DOMSignContext` is initialized with the private key and the document's root element. A `KeyValue` is created from the public key, and a `KeyInfo` object is constructed containing this key value. An `XMLSignature` object is created with the `SignedInfo` and `KeyInfo`, and the signature is applied to the document using the `sign` method. If an exception occurs during this process, it logs a warning message. The method returns the signed XML `Document`.
codeFunctions: public static Document sign (Document document,RSAPublicKey publicKey,RSAPrivateKey privateKey) { XMLSignatureFactory fac = XMLSignatureFactory.getInstance ("DOM");KeyInfoFactory keyInfoFactory = fac.getKeyInfoFactory ();try { Reference ref = fac.newReference ("",fac.newDigestMethod (DigestMethod.SHA1,null),Collections.singletonList (fac.newTransform (Transform.ENVELOPED,(TransformParameterSpec) null)),null,null);SignedInfo si = fac.newSignedInfo (fac.newCanonicalizationMethod (CanonicalizationMethod.INCLUSIVE,(C14NMethodParameterSpec) null),fac.newSignatureMethod (SignatureMethod.RSA_SHA1,null),Collections.singletonList (ref));DOMSignContext dsc = new DOMSignContext (privateKey,document.getDocumentElement ());KeyValue keyValue = keyInfoFactory.newKeyValue (publicKey);KeyInfo ki = keyInfoFactory.newKeyInfo (Collections.singletonList (keyValue));XMLSignature signature = fac.newXMLSignature (si,ki);signature.sign (dsc);} catch (Exception e) { logger.warn ("Error while signing an XML document.",e);} return document;}

originalComment: Check whether the given class is cache - safe in the given context i.e.whether it is loaded by the given ClassLoader or a parent of it.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `isCacheSafe` method checks if a given class is safe to cache in the context of a specified class loader. It ensures that the class loader of the provided class (`clazz`) is either the same as or a parent of the specified class loader (`classLoader`). If the class loader of `clazz` is `null`, or if it matches the specified class loader or any of its parent class loaders, the method returns `true`, indicating that the class is cache-safe. If a `SecurityException` is caught, typically due to restrictions in the system class loader, the method also returns `true`, assuming the class is safe. Otherwise, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isCacheSafe (Class <?> clazz,ClassLoader classLoader) { Preconditions.checkNotNull (clazz,"Class must not be null");try { ClassLoader target = clazz.getClassLoader ();if (target == null) { return true;} ClassLoader cur = classLoader;if (cur == target) { return true;} while (cur != null) { cur = cur.getParent ();if (cur == target) { return true;} } return false;} catch (SecurityException ex) { // Probably from the system ClassLoader - let's consider it safe. return true;} }

codeComment: This method, `resolvePrimitiveIfNecessary`, takes a `Class<?>` object as input and checks if it is a primitive type. If the class is a primitive type and not `void.class`, it returns the corresponding wrapper class from the `primitiveTypeToWrapperMap`. If the class is not a primitive type, it returns the original class. The method ensures that the input class is not null by using `Preconditions.checkNotNull`.
codeFunctions: public static Class <?> resolvePrimitiveIfNecessary (Class <?> clazz) { Preconditions.checkNotNull (clazz,"Class must not be null");return (clazz.isPrimitive () && clazz != void.class?primitiveTypeToWrapperMap.get (clazz):clazz);}

originalComment: Check if the right - hand side type may be assigned to the left - hand side type assuming setting by reflection.Considers primitive wrapper classes as assignable to the corresponding primitive types.
codeComment: The method `isAssignable` checks if the `rhsType` (right-hand side type) can be assigned to the `lhsType` (left-hand side type). It first ensures that neither `lhsType` nor `rhsType` is null. It then checks if `lhsType` is assignable from `rhsType` using the `isAssignableFrom` method. If `lhsType` is a primitive type, it looks up the corresponding wrapper class in `primitiveWrapperTypeMap` and checks if it matches `lhsType`. If `lhsType` is not a primitive, it looks up the corresponding primitive type in `primitiveTypeToWrapperMap` and checks if `lhsType` is assignable from this wrapper class. If any of these conditions are met, it returns true; otherwise, it returns false.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isAssignable (Class <?> lhsType,Class <?> rhsType) { Preconditions.checkNotNull (lhsType,"Left-hand side type must not be null");Preconditions.checkNotNull (rhsType,"Right-hand side type must not be null");if (lhsType.isAssignableFrom (rhsType)) { return true;} if (lhsType.isPrimitive ()) { Class <?> resolvedPrimitive = primitiveWrapperTypeMap.get (rhsType);if (resolvedPrimitive != null && lhsType.equals (resolvedPrimitive)) { return true;} } else { Class <?> resolvedWrapper = primitiveTypeToWrapperMap.get (rhsType);if (resolvedWrapper != null && lhsType.isAssignableFrom (resolvedWrapper)) { return true;} } return false;}

originalComment: Returns template variable name and value pairs extracted from the specified actual URI.
codeComment: The method `variables` takes a `String` parameter `uri` and returns a `Map<String, String>`. It initializes an empty `HashMap` called `variables`. It uses a `Matcher` object to match the `uri` against a predefined `pattern`. If the `uri` matches the pattern, it iterates over the groups found by the matcher (excluding the full match at index 0) and populates the `variables` map with keys from `this.variables` and values from the corresponding groups in the `uri`. Finally, it returns the populated `variables` map.
codeFunctions: public Map < String,String > variables (String uri) { Map < String,String > variables = new HashMap < String,String > ();Matcher matcher = pattern.matcher (uri);if (matcher.matches ()) { for (int i = 0;i < matcher.groupCount ();i ++) { variables.put (this.variables.get (i),matcher.group (i + 1));} } return variables;}

Depending on the raw type, it returns the default value for that primitive type: `false` for `boolean`, `0` for `char`, `byte`, `int`, and `short`, and `0.0` for `double` and `float`. originalComment: Converts the specified object to the specified user - defined value type.This method is overridable.You can provide your own conversion to the parameter construction by overriding this method.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `convertUserDefinedValueType` method attempts to convert a given `object` to a specified `type`. It first checks if the `object` is already an instance of the `type`. If not, and if the `object` is a `String`, it tries to convert the `String` to the `type` using one of two methods:
1. Invoking a constructor of the `type` that takes a `String` as an argument.
2. Invoking a static `valueOf` method of the `type` that takes a `String` as an argument.

If neither method succeeds, it logs a warning and returns `null`. If any exceptions occur during these attempts, they are caught, and debug information is logged.
codeFunctions: protected Object convertUserDefinedValueType (Object object,Class <?> type) { if (type.isAssignableFrom (object.getClass ())) { return object;} else if (object instanceof String) { try { Constructor <?> constructor = type.getConstructor (String.class);return constructor.newInstance (object);} catch (Exception e) { logger.debug ("Cannot invoke [public " + type.getName () + "(String.class)] constrcutor on [" + type + "]",e);} try { return type.getMethod ("valueOf",String.class).invoke (null,object);} catch (Exception e1) { logger.debug ("Cannot invoke [public static " + type.getName () + ".valueOf(String.class)]" + "method on [" + type + "]",e1);} } else { logger.warn ("Parameter [" + object + "] cannot be converted to [" + type + "]");} return null;}

originalComment: Returns the Web endpoint method parameter from query string.
codeComment: The `query` method is a protected method that takes a `Type` and a `String` as parameters and returns an `Object`. It uses the `parameter` method, passing in the `Type`, `String`, and two `Function` objects. The first `Function` retrieves a single parameter from the request using the provided name. The second `Function` retrieves a collection of parameters from the request that start with the provided name followed by an opening bracket `[`. If no such parameters are found, it returns `null`; otherwise, it returns the values of the parameters as a `Collection<Object>`.
codeFunctions: protected Object query (Type type,String name) { return parameter (type,name,new Function < String,Object > () { public Object apply (String name) { return context.request ().getParameter (name);} },new Function < String,Collection < Object > > () { @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public Collection < Object > apply (String name) { HttpServletRequest request = context.request ();Map < String,Object > map = new TreeMap < String,Object > ();for (Object object:Collections.list (request.getParameterNames ())) { String key = (String) object;if (key.startsWith (name + "[")) { map.put (key,request.getParameter (key));} } return (map.isEmpty ())?null:map.values ();} });}

originalComment: Returns the Web endpoint method parameter from cookie in the HTTP request.
codeComment:
The method `cookie` retrieves cookie values from an HTTP request based on the provided `type` and `name`. It uses two `Function` objects to handle different scenarios:

1. The first `Function` retrieves a single cookie value by name. It iterates through the cookies in the request, and if a cookie with the specified name is found, it returns the cookie's value. If no such cookie is found, it returns `null`.

2. The second `Function` retrieves multiple cookie values that start with the specified name followed by an opening bracket `[`. It collects these cookies into a `Map` where the keys are the cookie names and the values are the cookie values. It then returns the values of this map as a `Collection`. If no cookies match the criteria, it returns `null`.

The method `cookie` ultimately returns an `Object` which could be either a single cookie value (as a `String`) or a collection of cookie values (as a `Collection<Object>`), depending on the `type` parameter.
codeFunctions: protected Object cookie (Type type,String name) { return parameter (type,name,new Function < String,Object > () { public Object apply (String name) { Cookie [ ] cookies = context.request ().getCookies ();if (cookies != null) { for (Cookie cookie:cookies) { if (cookie.getName ().equals (name)) { return cookie.getValue ();} } } return null;} },new Function < String,Collection < Object > > () { public Collection < Object > apply (String name) { HttpServletRequest request = context.request ();Map < String,Object > map = new TreeMap < String,Object > ();Cookie [ ] cookies = request.getCookies ();if (cookies != null) { for (Cookie cookie:cookies) { String key = cookie.getName ();if (key.startsWith (name + "[")) { map.put (key,cookie.getValue ());} } } return (map.isEmpty ())?null:map.values ();} });}

originalComment: Returns the Web endpoint method parameter from HTTP session.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `session` method retrieves an attribute or a collection of attributes from the HTTP session based on the provided `type` and `name`. It uses two `Function` objects:
1. The first `Function` retrieves a single attribute from the session using the `name`.
2. The second `Function` retrieves a collection of attributes. If the attribute is already a `Collection`, it returns it directly. Otherwise, it constructs a `Map` of attributes whose keys start with the given `name` followed by `[`, and returns the values of this map. If no such attributes are found, it returns `null`.

The method `parameter` is called with these two functions to handle the retrieval logic based on the `type`.
codeFunctions: protected Object session (Type type,String name) { return parameter (type,name,new Function < String,Object > () { public Object apply (String name) { return context.session ().getAttribute (name);} },new Function < String,Collection < Object > > () { @ SuppressWarnings ("unchecked") public Collection < Object > apply (String name) { HttpSession session = context.session ();Object attribute = session.getAttribute (name);if (attribute instanceof Collection <?>) { return (Collection < Object >) attribute;} Map < String,Object > map = new TreeMap < String,Object > ();for (Object object:Collections.list (session.getAttributeNames ())) { String key = (String) object;if (key.startsWith (name + "[")) { map.put (key,session.getAttribute (key));} } return (map.isEmpty ())?null:map.values ();} });}

originalComment: Check if annotated result permissions contains all values from annotated array.Then it also check if all permissions in annotated method value array are granted.
codeComment:
The method `allValuesGranted` checks if all the permissions or permission strings provided in the `values` array have been granted according to the `resultMap`. It first checks if `values` is an array of `Permission` objects. If so, it converts the array to a `Set` and checks if all these permissions are present in the `resultMap`'s key set. It then iterates through each permission in `values` to ensure that each one has a `Result.GRANTED` status in the `resultMap`. If any permission is not granted, it logs the denial and returns `false`. If all permissions are granted, it returns `true`.

If `values` is an array of `String` objects, it converts the array to a `Set` of strings and checks if all these strings correspond to permissions present in the `resultMap`'s key set (converted to strings). It then iterates through each string in `values`, converts it to a `Permission` object, and checks if it has a `Result.GRANTED` status in the `resultMap`. If any permission is not granted, it logs the denial and returns `false`. If all permissions are granted, it returns `true`.

If `values` is neither an array of `Permission` objects nor an array of strings, the method returns `false`.
codeFunctions: private static boolean allValuesGranted (Object [ ] values,HashMap < Permission,Result > resultMap) { if (values instanceof Permission [ ]) { Set < Permission > valueSet = new HashSet <> (Arrays.asList ((Permission [ ]) values));if (resultMap.keySet ().containsAll (valueSet)) { for (Object value:values) { if (Result.GRANTED != resultMap.get ((Permission) value)) { mLog.i (TAG,"denied - " + value.toString ());return false;} } return true;} } else if (values instanceof String [ ]) { Set < String > valueSet = new HashSet <> (Arrays.asList ((String [ ]) values));Set < String > permission = new HashSet <> ();for (Permission perm:resultMap.keySet ()) { permission.add (perm.toString ());} if (permission.containsAll (valueSet)) { for (Object value:values) { if (Result.GRANTED != resultMap.get (Permission.get (String.valueOf (value)))) { mLog.i (TAG,"denied - " + value);return false;} } return true;} } return false;}

originalComment: Check if annotated result permissions contains all values from annotated array.Then it also check if any permission in annotated method value array is denied.
codeComment: The method `anyValueDenied` checks if any of the provided values are denied based on the results stored in a `resultMap`. It handles two types of input arrays: `Permission[]` and `String[]`. For `Permission[]`, it converts the array to a `LinkedHashSet` and checks if all permissions are present in the `resultMap`. If any permission is denied, it logs the denied permission and returns `true`. For `String[]`, it converts the array to a `HashSet` and checks against the string representations of the permissions in the `resultMap`. If any string corresponds to a denied permission, it logs the denied permission and returns `true`. If no denied permissions are found, it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: private static boolean anyValueDenied (Object [ ] values,HashMap < Permission,Result > resultMap) { if (values instanceof Permission [ ]) { Set < Permission > valueSet = new LinkedHashSet <> (Arrays.asList ((Permission [ ]) values));if (resultMap.keySet ().containsAll (valueSet)) { for (Object value:values) { if (Result.DENIED == resultMap.get ((Permission) value)) { mLog.i (TAG,"denied - " + value.toString ());return true;} } } } else if (values instanceof String [ ]) { Set < String > valueSet = new HashSet <> (Arrays.asList ((String [ ]) values));Set < String > permissionSet = new HashSet <> ();for (Permission perm:resultMap.keySet ()) { permissionSet.add (perm.toString ());} if (permissionSet.containsAll (valueSet)) { for (Object value:values) { if (Result.DENIED == resultMap.get (Permission.get ((String) value))) { mLog.i (TAG,"denied - " + value);return true;} } } } return false;}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `put` method overrides the superclass method to insert a key-value pair into a map. It first processes the queue to remove any entries that have been garbage collected. A new `SoftValue` object is created to wrap the value, associating it with the key and a reference queue. This `SoftValue` is then inserted into the map, and the method adds the value to strong references to prevent immediate garbage collection. If a previous value was associated with the key, it returns that value; otherwise, it returns `null`.
codeFunctions: @ Override public V put (K key,V value) { processQueue ();// throw out garbage collected values first SoftValue < V,K > sv = new SoftValue < V,K > (value,key,queue);SoftValue < V,K > previous = map.put (key,sv);addToStrongReferences (value);return previous != null?previous.get ():null;}

### Summary:
The `readArguments` method is a generic method that processes command-line arguments based on a provided interface class. It attempts to create an instance of the class that implements the given interface and processes the arguments using an `ArgumentHandler`. If there are any invalid arguments or if the user requests help, it prints an error message or usage instructions and returns `null`. Otherwise, it returns the configured instance of the class.
codeFunctions: public static < A > A readArguments (Class < A > interfaceClass,String [ ] args) { A result = null;try { final ArgumentHandler argumentHandler = new ArgumentHandler (args);result = argumentHandler.getInstance (interfaceClass);argumentHandler.processArguments (new ArgumentProcessor () { @ Override public void process (List < String > remaining) throws InvalidArgumentsException { if (remaining.size () > 0) { throw new InvalidArgumentsException ("The following arguments could not be understood: " + remaining);} } });} catch (InvalidArgumentsException e) { System.out.println (e.getMessage ());showUsage (interfaceClass);result = null;} if (result instanceof ArgumentsWithHelp) { if (((ArgumentsWithHelp) result).getHelp ()) { showUsage (interfaceClass);result = null;} } return result;}

### Summary:
The method `getAllProtbufFields` retrieves a map of fields annotated with `ProtobufAttribute` from a given class. It first checks if the map is already cached for the class. If cached, it returns the cached map. Otherwise, it initializes a new map, retrieves all fields of the class using `JReflectionUtils.getAllFields`, and iterates through them. For each field, it checks if the field is annotated with `ProtobufAttribute`. If it is, the field and its annotation are added to the map. Finally, the map is cached and returned.
codeFunctions: public static final Map < Field,ProtobufAttribute > getAllProtbufFields (Class <?extends Object > fromClazz) { Map < Field,ProtobufAttribute > protoBufFields = CLASS_TO_FIELD_MAP_CACHE.get (fromClazz.getCanonicalName ());if (protoBufFields != null) { return protoBufFields;} else { protoBufFields = new HashMap <> ();} final List < Field > fields = JReflectionUtils.getAllFields (new ArrayList < Field > (),fromClazz);for (Field field:fields) { final Annotation annotation = field.getAnnotation (ProtobufAttribute.class);if (annotation == null) { continue;} final ProtobufAttribute gpbAnnotation = (ProtobufAttribute) annotation;protoBufFields.put (field,gpbAnnotation);} // Caching to increase speed CLASS_TO_FIELD_MAP_CACHE.put (fromClazz.getCanonicalName (),protoBufFields);return protoBufFields;}

originalComment: Retrieve the getter against the Protobuf class;default is to is get plus upper case first character of the field name.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `getProtobufGetter` method generates a getter method name for a given `ProtobufAttribute` and `Field`. It first checks a cache (`CLASS_TO_FIELD_GETTERS_MAP_CACHE`) to see if the getter for the field has already been computed. If it is found in the cache, it returns the cached value. If not, it constructs the getter name by capitalizing the first letter of the field name and prefixing it with "get". If the field type is a `Collection`, it appends "List" to the getter name. If a custom getter is specified in the `protobufAttribute`, it returns that instead. Finally, it stores the computed getter in the cache and returns it.
codeFunctions: public static final String getProtobufGetter (ProtobufAttribute protobufAttribute,Field field) { final String fieldName = field.getName ();final String upperClassName = field.getDeclaringClass ().getCanonicalName ();// Look at the cache first Map < String,String > map = CLASS_TO_FIELD_GETTERS_MAP_CACHE.get (upperClassName);if (map != null) { if (!map.isEmpty () && map.containsKey (fieldName)) { return map.get (fieldName);} } else { map = new ConcurrentHashMap <> ();} final String upperCaseFirstFieldName = JStringUtils.upperCaseFirst (field.getName ());String getter = "get" + upperCaseFirstFieldName;if (Collection.class.isAssignableFrom (field.getType ())) { getter += "List";} if (!protobufAttribute.protobufGetter ().isEmpty ()) { return protobufAttribute.protobufGetter ();} map.put (fieldName,getter);CLASS_TO_FIELD_GETTERS_MAP_CACHE.put (upperClassName,map);return getter;}

codeFunctions: public static final String getPojoSetter (ProtobufAttribute protobufAttribute,Field field) { final String fieldName = field.getName ();final String upperClassName = field.getDeclaringClass ().getCanonicalName ();// Look at the cache first Map < String,String > map = CLASS_TO_FIELD_SETTERS_MAP_CACHE.get (upperClassName);if (map != null) { if (!map.isEmpty () && map.containsKey (fieldName)) { return map.get (fieldName);} } else { map = new ConcurrentHashMap <> ();} final String upperCaseFirstFieldName = JStringUtils.upperCaseFirst (field.getName ());String setter = "set" + upperCaseFirstFieldName;if (!protobufAttribute.pojoSetter ().isEmpty ()) { return protobufAttribute.pojoSetter ();} map.put (fieldName,setter);CLASS_TO_FIELD_SETTERS_MAP_CACHE.put (upperClassName,map);return setter;}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `toJson` method is a generic method that converts an object of any type `T` into a JSON string. It uses a `StringWriter` to capture the JSON output, a `JsonGenerator` to generate the JSON, and a `Mapper` to write the object's data into the JSON format. codeFunctions: public static ClassLoader getDefault () { ClassLoader loader = null;try { loader = Thread.currentThread ().getContextClassLoader ();} catch (Exception e) { } if (loader == null) { loader = ClassLoaderUtils.class.getClassLoader ();if (loader == null) { loader = ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader ();} } return loader;}

codeFunctions: public static URL getResource (String name,ClassLoader classLoader) { Validate.notNull (name,"resourceName must be not null");if (name.startsWith ("/")) { name = name.substring (1);} if (classLoader != null) { URL url = classLoader.getResource (name);if (url != null) { return url;} } ClassLoader loader = Thread.currentThread ().getContextClassLoader ();if (loader != null && loader != classLoader) { URL url = loader.getResource (name);if (url != null) { return url;} } return ClassLoader.getSystemResource (name);}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `initializePath` method processes a URI string to extract and validate the path, query string, and fragment components. It performs the following steps:

1. **Null Check**: Throws a `MalformedURIException` if the input URI string (`p_uriSpec`) is null.
2. **Path Extraction**: Iterates through the URI string to identify the path component, which ends at the first occurrence of a space or a query string marker (`?`). Validates each character to ensure it is either reserved or unreserved, and checks for valid escape sequences.
3. **Query String Extraction**: If a query string marker (`?`) is found, it continues parsing to extract the query string, which ends at the first occurrence of a space or a fragment marker (`#`). Similar validation checks are applied.
4. **Fragment Extraction**: If a fragment marker (`#`) is found, it extracts the fragment component until the end of the string, applying the same validation rules.

Throughout the process, the method throws a `MalformedURIException` if it encounters invalid characters or escape sequences. The extracted path, query string, and fragment are stored in the respective member variables (`m_path`, `m_queryString`, `m_fragment`).
codeFunctions: private void initializePath (String p_uriSpec) throws MalformedURIException { if (p_uriSpec == null) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Cannot initialize path from null string!");} int index = 0;int start = 0;int end = p_uriSpec.length ();char testChar = ' ';// path - everything up to query string or fragment while (index < end) { testChar = p_uriSpec.charAt (index);if (testChar == ' ' || testChar == ' ') { break;} // check for valid escape sequence if (testChar == ' ') { if (index + 2 >= end ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 1)) ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 2))) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Path contains invalid escape sequence!");} } else if (!isReservedCharacter (testChar) &&!isUnreservedCharacter (testChar)) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Path contains invalid character: " + testChar);} index ++;} m_path = p_uriSpec.substring (start,index);// query - starts with ? and up to fragment or end if (testChar == ' ') { index ++;start = index;while (index < end) { testChar = p_uriSpec.charAt (index);if (testChar == ' ') { break;} if (testChar == ' ') { if (index + 2 >= end ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 1)) ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 2))) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Query string contains invalid escape sequence!");} } else if (!isReservedCharacter (testChar) &&!isUnreservedCharacter (testChar)) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Query string contains invalid character:" + testChar);} index ++;} m_queryString = p_uriSpec.substring (start,index);} // fragment - starts with # if (testChar == ' ') { index ++;start = index;while (index < end) { testChar = p_uriSpec.charAt (index);if (testChar == ' ') { if (index + 2 >= end ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 1)) ||!isHex (p_uriSpec.charAt (index + 2))) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Fragment contains invalid escape sequence!");} } else if (!isReservedCharacter (testChar) &&!isUnreservedCharacter (testChar)) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Fragment contains invalid character:" + testChar);} index ++;} m_fragment = p_uriSpec.substring (start,index);} }

If both checks pass, it assigns the value of `p_scheme` to the `m_scheme` variable.
codeFunctions: private void setScheme (String p_scheme) throws MalformedURIException { if (p_scheme == null) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Cannot set scheme from null string!");} if (!isConformantSchemeName (p_scheme)) { throw new MalformedURIException ("The scheme is not conformant.");} m_scheme = p_scheme;//.toLowerCase(); }

codeComment: The method `setUserinfo` sets the `m_userinfo` field with the provided `p_userinfo` string, ensuring it adheres to specific URI formatting rules. If `p_userinfo` is `null`, `m_userinfo` is set to `null`. If `m_host` is `null`, a `MalformedURIException` is thrown. The method validates each character in `p_userinfo` to ensure it contains only valid characters, including alphanumerics, mark characters, escaped characters, and specific special characters (';', ':', '&', '=', '+', '$', ','). If an invalid escape sequence or character is found, a `MalformedURIException` is thrown. If all checks pass, `m_userinfo` is updated with `p_userinfo`.
codeFunctions: private void setUserinfo (String p_userinfo) throws MalformedURIException { if (p_userinfo == null) { m_userinfo = null;} else { if (m_host == null) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Userinfo cannot be set when host is null!");} // userinfo can contain alphanumerics, mark characters, escaped // and ';',':','&','=','+','$',',' int index = 0;int end = p_userinfo.length ();char testChar = ' ';while (index < end) { testChar = p_userinfo.charAt (index);if (testChar == ' ') { if (index + 2 >= end ||!isHex (p_userinfo.charAt (index + 1)) ||!isHex (p_userinfo.charAt (index + 2))) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Userinfo contains invalid escape sequence!");} } else if (!isUnreservedCharacter (testChar) && USERINFO_CHARACTERS.indexOf (testChar) == - 1) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Userinfo contains invalid character:" + testChar);} index ++;} } m_userinfo = p_userinfo;}

codeFunctions: private void setPort (int p_port) throws MalformedURIException { if (p_port >= 0 && p_port <= 65535) { if (m_host == null) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Port cannot be set when host is null!");} } else if (p_port != - 1) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Invalid port number!");} n_port = p_port;}

codeComment: The method `appendPath` takes a string `p_addToPath` and appends it to the existing `m_path` while ensuring the resulting path is a valid URI path. It first checks if `p_addToPath` is null or empty, in which case it returns immediately. If `p_addToPath` contains invalid characters, it throws a `MalformedURIException`. If `m_path` is null or empty, it sets `m_path` to `p_addToPath`, ensuring it starts with a '/'. If `m_path` already ends with a '/', it appends `p_addToPath` after removing any leading '/'. Otherwise, it appends `p_addToPath` with a preceding '/' if `p_addToPath` does not already start with one.
codeFunctions: private void appendPath (String p_addToPath) throws MalformedURIException { if (p_addToPath == null || p_addToPath.length () == 0) { return;} if (!isURIString (p_addToPath)) { throw new MalformedURIException ("Path contains invalid character!");} if (m_path == null || m_path.length () == 0) { if (p_addToPath.startsWith ("/")) { m_path = p_addToPath;} else { m_path = "/" + p_addToPath;} } else if (m_path.endsWith ("/")) { if (p_addToPath.startsWith ("/")) { m_path = m_path.concat (p_addToPath.substring (1));} else { m_path = m_path.concat (p_addToPath);} } else { if (p_addToPath.startsWith ("/")) { m_path = m_path.concat (p_addToPath);} else { m_path = m_path.concat ("/" + p_addToPath);} } }

originalComment: Set the query string for this URI.A non - null value is valid only if this is an URI conforming to the generic URI syntax and the path value is not null.
codeComment: The method `setQueryString` sets the query string of a URI. It first checks if the provided query string is `null`, in which case it sets the internal `m_queryString` to `null`. If the URI is not generic, it throws a `MalformedURIException`. It also throws the same exception if the path of the URI is `null` or if the query string contains invalid characters. codeComment:
### Summary:
The `setMuffin` method is designed to set or delete a muffin (a piece of data) identified by `strParam` with the value `strValue`. It interacts with a `PersistenceService` to manage the data. Here's a step-by-step breakdown:

1. **Initialization**: Initializes `FileContents` (`fc`) and `URL` (`url`) to `null`.
2. **URL Construction**: Attempts to create a `URL` using `m_strCodeBase` and `strParam`. If an exception occurs, the method returns immediately.
3. **FileContents Retrieval**: Tries to retrieve `FileContents` for the constructed URL. If an exception occurs (indicating no muffin exists), `fc` is set to `null`.
4. **FileContents Creation**: If `fc` is `null`, it creates a new `FileContents` with a maximum length of 100 bytes and retrieves it again.
5. **Data Writing/Deletion**:
   - If `strValue` is not `null`, it writes the bytes of `strValue` (encoded in `ENCODING`) to the output stream of `fc` without appending, then closes the stream and marks the `FileContents` as dirty.
   - If `strValue` is `null`, it deletes the `FileContents` associated with the URL.
6. **Exception Handling**: Catches and prints any exceptions that occur during the process.

This method effectively manages the creation, updating, and deletion of muffins using a persistence service.

### Summary:
The `parseQuery` method is a generic method that takes a JSON response string and a class type `T` as input. It attempts to parse the JSON string into an object of type `T` using a `MAPPER` (presumably an instance of `ObjectMapper` from the Jackson library). If parsing fails due to `JsonParseException`, `JsonMappingException`, or `IOException`, it tries to parse the response into an `ErrorResponse` object instead. If parsing the error response also fails, it logs the error and returns `null`. If parsing the original response is successful, it returns the parsed object of type `T`.
codeFunctions:
private < T > T parseQuery (final String response,final Class < T > responseClass) { T queryResponse;try { /*
			 * Possible exceptions:
			 *
			 * IOException - if the underlying input source has problems during parsing
			 *
			 * JsonParseException - if parser has problems parsing content
			 *
			 * JsonMappingException - if the parser does not have any more content to map (note: Json "null" value is considered content; enf-of-stream not)
			 */ queryResponse = MAPPER.readValue (response,responseClass);} catch (JsonParseException | JsonMappingException e) { try { final ErrorResponse error = MAPPER.readValue (response,ErrorResponse.class);LOGGER.error ("Query returned an error: {}",error);return null;} catch (final IOException e1) { LOGGER.error ("Failed to read error response.",e1);} LOGGER.error ("Error reading response.",e);return null;} catch (final IOException e) { LOGGER.error ("Error reading response.",e);return null;} return queryResponse;}

The iterator maintains three indices: `iteratorIndex` to track the overall position, `iteratorBufferIndex` to track the current buffer, and `iteratorOffset` to track the position within the current buffer. The `hasNext()` method checks if there are more elements to iterate over by comparing `iteratorIndex` with the total size. originalComment: Parses a sql with named parameters.The parameter - index mappings are put into the map and the parsed sql is returned.
codeComment:
### Summary:
The `parseNamedSql` method processes a SQL string to replace named parameters with question marks (`?`). It maintains a map (`nameIndexMap`) that associates each named parameter with a list of indices where it appears in the SQL string. The method handles SQL strings that may contain quoted sections, ensuring that parameter-like strings within quotes are ignored. It iterates through the SQL string, identifies named parameters, and constructs a new SQL string with question marks in place of the named parameters. The method also updates the `nameIndexMap` with the positions of each named parameter.
codeFunctions: private static String parseNamedSql (String sql,Map < String,List < Integer > > nameIndexMap) { // I was originally using regular expressions, but they didn't work well for ignoring // parameter-like strings inside quotes. int length = sql.length ();StringBuffer parsedSql = new StringBuffer (length);boolean inSingleQuote = false;boolean inDoubleQuote = false;int index = 1;for (int i = 0;i < length;i ++) { char c = sql.charAt (i);if (inSingleQuote) { if (c == ' ') { inSingleQuote = false;} } else if (inDoubleQuote) { if (c == ' ') { inDoubleQuote = false;} } else { if (c == ' ') { inSingleQuote = true;} else if (c == ' ') { inDoubleQuote = true;} else if (c == ' ' && i + 1 < length && Character.isJavaIdentifierStart (sql.charAt (i + 1))) { int j = i + 2;while (j < length && Character.isJavaIdentifierPart (sql.charAt (j))) { j ++;} String name = sql.substring (i + 1,j);c = ' ';// replace the parameter with a question mark i += name.length ();// skip past the end if the parameter List < Integer > indexList = nameIndexMap.get (name);if (indexList == null) { indexList = new LinkedList < Integer > ();nameIndexMap.put (name,indexList);} indexList.add (index);index ++;} } parsedSql.append (c);} return parsedSql.toString ();}

The method waits for each process to complete and checks for any exceptions. If an `IOException` is encountered, it logs the error and rethrows the exception to indicate that the connection may need recovery. Other exceptions are logged as warnings. If an `InterruptedException` occurs while waiting for a process to complete, it logs the interruption.

### Summary:
The `matchTokens` method checks if an array of tokens matches a given array of patterns, where patterns can include wildcards and the special token `PATH_MATCH` (represented as `**`). The method performs the following steps:

1. **Initial Matching from Start:**
   - It iterates from the start of both the `tokens` and `patterns` arrays.
   - If a pattern element is `PATH_MATCH`, it breaks out of the loop.
   - If a token does not match the corresponding pattern (using `WildcharUtils.match`), it returns `false`.
   - It increments both the pattern and token indices.

2. **Check for Remaining Tokens:**
   - If all tokens are matched but there are remaining patterns, it checks if all remaining patterns are `PATH_MATCH`.
   - If not, it returns `false`.

3. **Initial Matching from End:**
   - It iterates from the end of both the `tokens` and `patterns` arrays.
   - If a pattern element is `PATH_MATCH`, it breaks out of the loop.
   - If a token does not match the corresponding pattern, it returns `false`.
   - It decrements both the pattern and token indices.

4. **Check for Remaining Tokens:**
   - If all tokens are matched but there are remaining patterns, it checks if all remaining patterns are `PATH_MATCH`.
   - If not, it returns `false`.

5. **Matching with `PATH_MATCH` in Between:**
   - It handles the case where `PATH_MATCH` appears in the middle of the patterns.
   - It searches for the next `PATH_MATCH` in the patterns.
   - It skips consecutive `PATH_MATCH` elements.
   - It attempts to match the sequence of patterns between two `PATH_MATCH` elements with a corresponding sequence in the tokens.
   - If no match is found, it returns `false`.
   - It updates the indices to continue the process.

6. **Final Check:**
   - After processing, it checks if any remaining patterns are not `PATH_MATCH`.
   - If so, it returns `false`.
   - Otherwise, it returns `true`, indicating a successful match.

1;while (patNdxStart <= patNdxEnd && tokNdxStart <= tokNdxEnd) { // find first ** String patDir = patterns [ patNdxStart ];if (patDir.equals (PATH_MATCH)) { break;} if (!WildcharUtils.match (tokens [ tokNdxStart ],patDir)) { return false;} patNdxStart ++;tokNdxStart ++;} if (tokNdxStart > tokNdxEnd) { for (int i = patNdxStart;i <= patNdxEnd;i ++) { // string is finished if (!patterns [ i ].equals (PATH_MATCH)) { return false;} } return true;} if (patNdxStart > patNdxEnd) { return false;// string is not finished, but pattern is } while (patNdxStart <= patNdxEnd && tokNdxStart <= tokNdxEnd) { // to the last ** String patDir = patterns [ patNdxEnd ];if (patDir.equals (PATH_MATCH)) { break;} if (!WildcharUtils.match (tokens [ tokNdxEnd ],patDir)) { return false;} patNdxEnd --;tokNdxEnd --;} if (tokNdxStart > tokNdxEnd) { for (int i = patNdxStart;i <= patNdxEnd;i ++) { // string is finished if (!patterns [ i ].equals (PATH_MATCH)) { return false;} } return true;} while ((patNdxStart != patNdxEnd) && (tokNdxStart <= tokNdxEnd)) { int patIdxTmp = - 1;for (int i = patNdxStart + 1;i <= patNdxEnd;i ++) { if (patterns [ i ].equals (PATH_MATCH)) { patIdxTmp = i;break;} } if (patIdxTmp == patNdxStart + 1) { patNdxStart ++;// skip **/** situation continue;} // find the pattern between padIdxStart & padIdxTmp in str between strIdxStart & strIdxEnd int patLength = (patIdxTmp - patNdxStart - 1);int strLength = (tokNdxEnd - tokNdxStart + 1);int ndx = - 1;strLoop:for (int i = 0;i <= strLength - patLength;i ++) { for (int j = 0;j < patLength;j ++) { String subPat = patterns [ patNdxStart + j + 1 ];String subStr = tokens [ tokNdxStart + i + j ];if (!WildcharUtils.match (subStr,subPat)) { continue strLoop;} } ndx = tokNdxStart + i;break;} if (ndx == - 1) { return false;} patNdxStart = patIdxTmp;tokNdxStart = ndx + patLength;} for (int i = patNdxStart;i <= patNdxEnd;i ++) { if (!patterns [ i ].equals (PATH_MATCH)) { return false;} } return true;}

If the column index `col` is less than the `width`, it iterates through the `cols` array up to the specified column, summing the values to determine the offset. If `col` is equal to `width`, it returns the width of the absolute position using `abspos.getWidth()`. If `col` exceeds `width`, it throws an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` with a message indicating the invalid column index.
codeFunctions: public int getColOfs (int col) throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException { if (col < width) { int ofs = 0;for (int i = 0;i < col;i ++) ofs += cols [ i ];return ofs;} else if (col == width) return abspos.getWidth ();else throw new ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (col + ">" + width);}

It takes an integer `row` as input and returns an integer representing the offset. The method checks if the `row` is less than `height`. If true, it calculates the offset by summing up the values in the `rows` array up to the specified `row`. If `row` equals `height`, it returns the height of `abspos`. If `row` is greater than `height`, it throws an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` with a message indicating the invalid row index.
codeFunctions: public int getRowOfs (int row) throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException { if (row < height) { int ofs = 0;for (int i = 0;i < row;i ++) ofs += rows [ i ];return ofs;} else if (row == height) return abspos.getHeight ();else throw new ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (row + ">" + height);}

codeComment: The method `getCellBoundsRelative` calculates and returns the bounds of a cell in a grid relative to its position. It takes two integer parameters, `x` and `y`, representing the column and row indices of the cell, respectively. The method first determines the top-left corner of the cell using the `getColOfs` and `getRowOfs` methods for the x and y coordinates. It then calculates the bottom-right corner of the cell. If the cell is in the last column (`x == width - 1`), the x-coordinate of the bottom-right corner is set to the width of `abspos` minus one. Otherwise, it is calculated as the sum of the x-coordinate of the top-left corner and the width of the column at index `x` minus one. Similarly, if the cell is in the last row (`y == height - 1`), the y-coordinate of the bottom-right corner is set to the height of `abspos` minus one. Otherwise, it is calculated as the sum of the y-coordinate of the top-left corner and the height of the row at index `y` minus one. Finally, the method returns a new `Rectangular` object representing the bounds of the cell with the calculated coordinates.
codeFunctions: public Rectangular getCellBoundsRelative (int x,int y) { int x1 = getColOfs (x);int y1 = getRowOfs (y);int x2 = (x == width - 1)?abspos.getWidth () - 1:x1 + cols [ x ] - 1;int y2 = (y == height - 1)?abspos.getHeight () - 1:y1 + rows [ y ] - 1;return new Rectangular (x1,y1,x2,y2);}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `calculateColumns` method performs the following tasks:
1. **Creates a Sorted List of Points**: It generates a list of `GridPoint` objects from the `areas` list, marking the start and end of each area. The points are then sorted.
2. **Calculates the Number of Columns**: By iterating through the sorted points, it counts the number of unique column positions, ensuring that the end of one area aligns with the start of another.
3. **Calculates Column Widths and Layout**: It calculates the width of each column and sets the X1 and X2 positions for each area in the `target` layout. It also tracks the maximum and minimum indentation levels.
4. **Final Adjustments**: If the last column does not align with the end of the area, it adjusts the column width accordingly. If no indentation is found, it sets the minimum indentation to 0.
codeFunctions: private void calculateColumns () { //create the sorted list of points GridPoint points [ ] = new GridPoint [ areas.size () * 2 ];int pi = 0;for (Area area:areas) { points [ pi ] = new GridPoint (area.getX1 (),area,true);points [ pi + 1 ] = new GridPoint (area.getX2 () + 1,area,false);pi += 2;//X2+1 ensures that the end of one box will be on the same point //as the start of the following box } Arrays.sort (points);//calculate the number of columns int cnt = 0;int last = abspos.getX1 ();for (int i = 0;i < points.length;i ++) if (!theSame (points [ i ].value,last)) { last = points [ i ].value;cnt ++;} if (!theSame (last,abspos.getX2 ())) cnt ++;//last column finishes the whole area width = cnt;//calculate the column widths and the layout maxindent = 0;minindent = - 1;cols = new int [ width ];cnt = 0;last = abspos.getX1 ();for (int i = 0;i < points.length;i ++) { if (!theSame (points [ i ].value,last)) { cols [ cnt ] = points [ i ].value - last;last = points [ i ].value;cnt ++;} if (points [ i ].begin) { target.getPosition (points [ i ].area).setX1 (cnt);maxindent = cnt;if (minindent == - 1) minindent = maxindent;//points[i].node.getArea().setX1(parent.getArea().getX1() + getColOfs(cnt)); } else { Rectangular pos = target.getPosition (points [ i ].area);pos.setX2 (cnt - 1);if (pos.getX2 () < pos.getX1 ()) pos.setX2 (pos.getX1 ());//points[i].node.getArea().setX2(parent.getArea().getX1() + getColOfs(pos.getX2()+1)); } } if (!theSame (last,abspos.getX2 ())) cols [ cnt ] = abspos.getX2 () - last;if (minindent == - 1) minindent = 0;}

codeComment:
### Summary:
The `calculateRows` method performs the following tasks:
1. **Creates a Sorted List of Points**: It initializes an array of `GridPoint` objects, where each `Area` in the `areas` list contributes two points: one for the start (`getY1()`) and one for the end (`getY2() + 1`) of the area. The points are then sorted.
2. **Calculates the Number of Rows**: It iterates through the sorted points to count the number of unique row positions, ensuring that the end of one area aligns with the start of another if necessary.
3. **Calculates Row Heights and Layout**: It calculates the height of each row by determining the difference between consecutive unique row positions. It also updates the `y1` and `y2` positions of each area in the `target` layout based on these row calculations.

This method effectively organizes areas into rows and calculates their respective heights and positions within a given layout.
codeFunctions: private void calculateRows () { //create the sorted list of points GridPoint points [ ] = new GridPoint [ areas.size () * 2 ];int pi = 0;for (Area area:areas) { points [ pi ] = new GridPoint (area.getY1 (),area,true);points [ pi + 1 ] = new GridPoint (area.getY2 () + 1,area,false);pi += 2;//Y2+1 ensures that the end of one box will be on the same point //as the start of the following box } Arrays.sort (points);//calculate the number of rows int cnt = 0;int last = abspos.getY1 ();for (int i = 0;i < points.length;i ++) if (!theSame (points [ i ].value,last)) { last = points [ i ].value;cnt ++;} if (!theSame (last,abspos.getY2 ())) cnt ++;//last row finishes the whole area height = cnt;//calculate the row heights and the layout rows = new int [ height ];cnt = 0;last = abspos.getY1 ();for (int i = 0;i < points.length;i ++) { if (!theSame (points [ i ].value,last)) { rows [ cnt ] = points [ i ].value - last;last = points [ i ].value;cnt ++;} if (points [ i ].begin) { target.getPosition (points [ i ].area).setY1 (cnt);//points[i].node.getArea().setY1(parent.getArea().getY1() + getRowOfs(cnt)); } else { Rectangular pos = target.getPosition (points [ i ].area);pos.setY2 (cnt - 1);if (pos.getY2 () < pos.getY1 ()) pos.setY2 (pos.getY1 ());//points[i].node.getArea().setY2(parent.getArea().getY1() + getRowOfs(pos.getY2()+1)); } } if (!theSame (last,abspos.getY2 ())) rows [ cnt ] = abspos.getY2 () - last;}
